training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.rationale: Training is a job that exits; serving is a process that must stay up. They differ in resource shape (a fit spikes memory, an inference does not), in scaling (train scales to zero, serving needs a warm replica), and in failure handling (a job retries, a service must stay available). Running a fit inside the serving process couples them at the worst point: the fit's memory spike is charged to the same cgroup as the live model cache, so a retrain can OOM-kill the endpoint that is currently answering. The trainer image also carries fit-time dependencies a serving process never calls, which is dead weight on every cold start.
training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.consequence: POST /retrain never fits anything itself. It records intent and returns; the existing trainer image does the work, spawned the same way MODEL-FLOW-003-T04 already spawns it.
training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.scope_correction: NARROWED 2026-08-25. This decision remains right for a long-running synchronous serving process (MODEL-SERVE-002) and for never fitting inside one. It was over-applied when written: it was read as 'inference always needs its own image', and scheduled batch inference is a counterexample its own rationale does not cover. See short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference. MODEL-SERVE-002-T01 (a separate serving image) is unaffected and stays.

deploy_is_a_row_change_not_an_image_buil.chosen: One generic serving image; the production pointer lives in Postgres
deploy_is_a_row_change_not_an_image_buil.rationale: The alternative — one image per model — makes every retrain a CI run and every rollback a redeploy, and turns N models into N deployments to operate. Since the model is data the process loads, not code it links against, the version in production is a fact about a row. Promotion becomes an UPDATE and rollback becomes the same UPDATE in reverse, which is what makes rollback fast enough to actually use during an incident.

short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.chosen: Short-lived containers on the existing trainer image, second entrypoint
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.rationale: REVISES the scope of training_and_serving_are_separate_planes rather than contradicting it. That decision's reason is specific: a FIT spikes memory and, sharing a cgroup with a long-running cache, can OOM-kill the endpoint currently answering. Hourly batch inference is not a long-running process and holds no cache, so that reason does not apply to it. What is left is a comparison the existing code wins outright — trainning-container.authorized.service.ts already spawns, resource-limits and reaps containers; ModelTrainingRunLog and the /log callback already give per-run logs; image_digest provenance already comes for free. A second entrypoint (infer.py) beside train.py in images/trainer/ reuses all of it. Cold start is a python import, 3-5s, which is noise at a one-hour cadence.
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.consequence: MODEL-SERVE-006 needs no serving process, no cache-invalidation-on-promote, and no readiness protocol. Those belong to MODEL-SERVE-002 (synchronous /predict) alone, which is a SEPARATE requirement arriving later — do not build a serving service in order to get an hourly run.
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.also: One image, not two, additionally removes a divergence risk the two-image plan created: both entrypoints unpickle the same model.joblib, so they cannot disagree about the library that wrote it.

metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.chosen: predictions.parquet is the source of truth; metrics.json is a cache
metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.rationale: The alternative — the client sends a metric set and the container computes exactly those — has one failure that gets worse over time: adding a metric next month leaves every existing run without it, so a comparison table shows a column of em-dashes, and the only way to fill it is to RETRAIN models in order to compute a number that never needed a fit. Deriving from the stored predictions instead means a new metric is recomputable across all history, and the same definitions serve both evaluation (test-split predictions) and monitoring (inference predictions) — one implementation, so 'r2 at training' and 'r2 in monitoring' cannot drift into two numbers that look comparable and are not.
metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.constraint: STATE THE BOUNDARY EXPLICITLY IN THE REGISTRY. Only metrics computable from (actual, predicted) plus scalars already in run_manifest.json (e.g. feature_count for adjusted R²) are backfillable. Anything needing feature values, residual-vs-feature structure or model internals is NOT, and must be marked so — otherwise the registry mixes metrics that can be added retroactively with metrics that cannot, in one table, and nobody can tell which is which.

ORIGINAL, PRESERVED: 'NEW 2026-09-01, OPENED BY MODEL-SERVE-000-T07, NOT RESOLVED HERE — an audit surfaces the tension, MODEL-SERVE-001 decides it. But DS-LAKE-025's `adopt_artifact`... is live, working precedent for the OPPOSITE principle... Both are correct in their own scope and they point opposite directions on the same question.'
open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_byt.rationale: The two precedents are not actually in tension once the difference in what each one is protecting is named. DS-LAKE-025 copies bytes OUT OF `drafts/` because the SOURCE prefix (a DatasetDraft's own workspace) is reclaimable — a dataset draft's sweeper can and does delete `drafts/{draftId}/...` once abandoned, so the saved Dataset must own independent bytes or a later reclaim takes it down. MODEL-SERVE-000-T07 measured the opposite fact for models: the FINAL artifact every run trains against is ALREADY unconditionally excluded from the cleanup candidate query (`artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts`'s `where: { type: { not: 'FINAL' } }`), and an adopted run's own prefix (`drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/...`) is protected by MODEL-FLOW-011-T05's adopted-run guard. There is no reclaimable source for a copy to protect against — copying would duplicate storage against a risk that does not exist, and it would violate MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's adopt-by-pointer rule for the same reason that rule exists on the training side: the row records what happened, it is not a workspace, and a copy is a second, driftable copy of facts the run row already owns.

Revisit ONLY if a future change makes FINAL artifacts or adopted-run prefixes reclaimable while a ModelVersion still references them — at which point this decision inherits DS-LAKE-025's own reasoning instead of contradicting it.

open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_byt.implementation: `ModelVersion.goldArtifactId/goldObjectKey/artifactChecksum/featureSpecKey/modelObjectKey` are copied as STRING KEYS from `ModelTrainingRun`'s own pinned columns at version-creation time (one hop, per MODEL-SERVE-000-T03/T07) — the row never re-derives through the dataset's current artifact, and it never fetches or duplicates the underlying bytes.

serving_cache_staleness_bound.verification: MODEL-SERVE-002-V02 promotes under continuous /predict load and asserts every response is answerable by some valid version with the switchover landing inside this bound.

batch_worker_is_a_trainer_image_mode.chosen: A new MODE=batch on the existing images/trainer/ image — a short-lived container, not the apps/serving process.
batch_worker_is_a_trainer_image_mode.rationale: Decided WITH THE USER before implementation. Matches decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference's own reasoning: a batch score is not a long-running process and holds no cache, so training_and_serving_are_separate_planes's OOM-kill-the-live-endpoint concern does not apply to it. The container gets the strongest available memory isolation (its own 8GiB cgroup cap, ReadonlyRootfs, tmpfs /scratch) rather than sharing a cgroup with apps/serving's live model LRU cache. It also reuses, rather than reinvents, everything trainning-container.authorized.service.ts already provides: spawn/watch/reap, per-row reconcileOrphanedRuns()-style restart recovery, resource limits, and image_digest provenance.

rejected.apps/serving file-scoring endpoint: Rejected: a batch score run inside the serving process is charged to the SAME cgroup as the live model cache MODEL-SERVE-002 built — a wide batch input can pressure memory the same way a fit does, which is the exact coupling training_and_serving_are_separate_planes exists to prevent, just moved one layer down. It would also need the serving process to hold job state, and it is deliberately credential-free (no DB, no S3 creds) — confirmed live: apps/serving/requirements.txt has no psycopg/minio/boto3/prisma.
rejected.backend chunks into the existing synchro: Rejected: N HTTP round trips per batch (one per SERVING_MAX_ROWS-sized chunk), still loads the live serving process anyway, and requires apps/backend (Node) to read and write parquet, which no code in this repo does today. Output assembly in Node is also exactly the memory risk T03 warns about, moved into the wrong process.

batch_worker_is_a_trainer_image_mode.cost_accepted: images/trainer/ cannot apply the training-time scaling transform today (no to_model_ready, no softsensor_scaling — confirmed live, zero matches). Its build context is images/trainer/ only. This decision requires adding the extracted package as a dependency AND moving that build context to the repo root, mirroring the move apps/serving/Dockerfile already made for the same reason. Checked before accepting this cost: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile (docs/feature_list.json:179, verified verbatim), so the move breaks no pipeline — only the manual build command changes.

batch_input_is_pre_scale.chosen: The batch input parquet carries the model's feature columns in raw engineering units — the identical contract MODEL-SERVE-002's synchronous /predict already uses. The worker applies the fitted scaling transform (softsensor_scaling.to_model_ready) before predicting.
batch_input_is_pre_scale.rationale: Decided WITH THE USER. One request contract for both the synchronous and batch paths, rather than two. Critically avoids the silent-wrong-answer trap this ledger repeatedly guards against (the empty-scaling-array trap, MODEL-SERVE-000-T03's highest-severity finding): under this contract, supplying raw values is the CORRECT thing to do, not a mistake that produces a plausible wrong number with no error. The rejected alternative (an already-scaled, GOLD-shaped input) would make the batch contract differ from /predict's for the same model and would require the caller to obtain scalingParams themselves to pre-scale it — reintroducing exactly the class of silent failure MODEL-SERVE-002-T05 was built to close.
batch_input_is_pre_scale.consequence: pipelines/batch.py must call softsensor_scaling.assert_scaling_coverage before transforming, the same guard rows_to_predictions applies in apps/serving/services/predict.py — one shared function, not two implementations that could drift.

findings: CORRECTED 2026-08-24 FROM A MINIO SCREENSHOT OF A REAL RUN (bucket `datasets`, key drafts/1ce30923-394b-4135-b324-0e913606dcf9/runs/61f9aa28-0c31-4e99-bd52-4674200f72f6/, timestamps 2026-08-19 11:44 — one of the two runs MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 live-verified). The prior finding called the run's descriptor `manifest.json`; the object is `run_manifest.json`. The rename is not cosmetic: the name scopes it to the RUN, and a run descriptor and a serving descriptor are not the same document. A run manifest records what happened during a fit; serving needs what is required to LOAD the result. They may overlap, but assuming they are identical is exactly the kind of assumption MODEL-SERVE-000 exists to stop. Contents remain UNVERIFIED — the screenshot shows names and sizes only.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03). ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NEW AND HIGHEST SEVERITY IN THIS LEDGER — THE RUN DIRECTORY IS NOT A SELF-CONTAINED SERVING BUNDLE, CONFIRMED BY OBSERVATION. The directory holds exactly four objects: metrics.json (155 B), model.joblib (1.1 KiB), predictions.parquet (24.9 KiB), run_manifest.json (1.2 KiB). There is NO feature_spec.json and NO scaler or preprocessor object. model.joblib at 1.1 KiB is corroborating evidence rather than proof, but it is strong: a fitted sklearn Pipeline carrying a scaler's own state does not serialise to a kilobyte — this is an estimator alone. So a serving process cannot open this prefix and predict. It must resolve Model -> ModelTrainingRun -> DatasetArtifact.featureSpecKey -> feature_spec.json, three hops across two entities, and the transform state (scalers, the effective column list from select_columns + force_keep_target) lives at the far end of that chain on an entity the USER CAN EDIT.' THE 'THREE HOPS' CLAIM IS WRONG — read from packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma:1006-1031: ModelTrainingRun carries goldArtifactId, goldObjectKey, artifactChecksum AND featureSpecKey directly on the run row, set at launch from the ARTIFACT the run was actually created against (model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:126, `featureSpecKey: artifact.featureSpecKey`) — never re-derived through the dataset's current artifact. Verified against the live dev database: 0 of 73 ModelTrainingRun rows have a null featureSpecKey. So this is ONE hop off the run row (ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey -> feature_spec.json), not three hops through an editable dataset. The 'not co-located, so a correct implementation can still be fed the wrong spec' exposure the finding worried about does not exist: the pinned key cannot silently repoint to an edited dataset's current artifact.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T07). ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NEW — NOTHING PINS OR PROTECTS THE ARTIFACT A MODEL WAS FITTED AGAINST. MODEL-FLOW-010's own finding states that editing a dataset keeps the Dataset id and moves currentArtifactId, and correctly concludes that ModelDraft.datasetId stays valid. That conclusion is right for the WIZARD and wrong to inherit here: a served model needs the SPECIFIC artifact it was fitted against, not the dataset's current one, and neither ledger says that artifact is retained for as long as a model references it. Two separate objects can therefore be reclaimed out from under one production model — its bytes (guarded upstream by MODEL-FLOW-011-T05) and its feature spec (guarded by nothing). Losing either is the same outage.' WRONG ON BOTH CLAUSES, verified against schema.prisma and the live dev DB/MinIO. PINNING: ModelTrainingRun already carries goldArtifactId, goldObjectKey, artifactChecksum and featureSpecKey — an id-only reference was never the design (see schema.prisma:1019-1031's own comment: 'NOT how the container resolves data ... an id-only reference would silently retrain on different rows later'). PROTECTION: measured live — ALL 73 ModelTrainingRun rows train against a FINAL artifact, zero against GOLD. `artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts`'s candidate query (`where: { type: { not: 'FINAL' } }`) and `artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts:236` (`if (artifact.type === 'FINAL') continue`) both exclude FINAL unconditionally — it is never a cleanup candidate. Post-DS-LAKE-025, FINAL owns its bytes outright at `{datasetId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/` with feature_spec.json copied alongside (`adopt_artifact`, artifact_service.py:1268). 0 of 61 SUCCEEDED runs point at a missing or objectReclaimedAt-stamped artifact (measured). TWO REAL EXPOSURES SURVIVE, NEITHER THE ONE ORIGINALLY CLAIMED: (1) the FINAL protection is a TYPE EXCLUSION, not a ModelTrainingRun reference check — nothing but PreprocessingJob (QUEUED/RUNNING) counts as a live reference in the cleanup sweep, and `artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts:314-324` explicitly allows GOLD/SILVER to age out 'even if still lineage-reachable', reasoning that an unreached one is storage 'nothing can ever reclaim and nothing reads' — false the moment a ModelTrainingRun points at it, which no launch path currently forbids. Latent, not live, today. (2) `deleteDatasetService` (apps/backend/src/api/v1/dataset/authorized/dataset.authorized.service.ts:234-246) checks ownership only, then `prisma.dataset.delete` — Dataset cascades onto DatasetArtifact (schema.prisma:563), and ModelTrainingRun.goldArtifactId is a bare String with no FK, so it dangles silently. Bytes still resolve (goldObjectKey/featureSpecKey are pinned keys, not FKs), but the objects become permanently unreclaimable — cleanup enumerates DatasetArtifact rows, and the row is gone. UPSTREAM TICKETS NAMED, NOT WRITTEN HERE: deleteDatasetService should refuse or warn when a ModelTrainingRun references the dataset's artifacts; the cleanup sweep's live-reference set should include ModelTrainingRun.goldArtifactId before any launch path can target a non-FINAL artifact.

NEW — ONE BUCKET HOLDS EVERYTHING. Model run outputs live in the `datasets` bucket (17.4 MiB / 138 objects at the time of the screenshot). That is fine today and cheap to leave alone, but it means no bucket-scoped lifecycle rule, retention policy or access grant can distinguish a production model's bytes from an abandoned dataset draft's. Anyone who later writes a lifecycle rule intending it for datasets writes it for models too. Record it now so that decision is made deliberately rather than discovered.

NEW AND USEFUL — MODEL-SERVE-002-V01 IS RUNNABLE TODAY. predictions.parquet exists in the run directory (24.9 KiB), so the no-skew test — score a row from the model's own test split through the live endpoint and assert it matches the recorded prediction — has real reference data against a real fitted model, with no live wizard and no MODEL-FLOW-007 required. NEW — NO CHECKSUM SIDECAR EXISTS. There is no .sha256 or equivalent object beside model.joblib, so a checksum either lives inside run_manifest.json or is not computed at all. MODEL-SERVE-000-T01 must distinguish those two, because they lead to different work: reading a field, versus adding a write to the trainer AND accepting that every artifact predating that change has no checksum and needs a stated policy.

CONFIRMED 2026-08-24 by reading run_manifest.json from the run in the screenshot. The prior finding, and MODEL-SERVE-000-T01's three questions, are now answered and the finding is REPLACED rather than deleted so the audit trail survives: (1) a checksum EXISTS — model_sha256, plus artifact_checksum for the GOLD parquet; (2) provenance is pinned by image_digest (scgc/soft-sensor-trainer@sha256:…), which is STRONGER than the sklearn/joblib version string this ledger asked for, because it pins the whole runtime rather than one library; (3) the manifest does NOT carry a featureSpecKey, but it DOES inline feature_columns, target_y, target_scaled and derived_from_target — four of the fields serving would otherwise have walked to the spec for. seed and the full split record (method, ratio, cut_timestamp, labelled/train/test rows) are also present. CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03), PREMISE INVERTED. ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NARROWED 2026-08-24 — THE ONLY MISSING SERVING INPUT IS SCALER STATE. With feature_columns inlined, the three-hop chain to feature_spec.json collapses to one open question rather than a general dependency: where does a run's SCALER configuration live, and is it recoverable at serve time? The manifest records target_scaled: false, which proves the system tracks scaling on the target side, and records nothing about the feature side. model.joblib at 1.1 KiB for a bare 8-feature OLS is consistent with this particular run having no scalers at all — which is why it cannot answer the question. MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 must therefore be run against a run that DID scale, not this one; the smallest, cleanest artifact is the least informative one here.' SCALER STATE IS NOT MISSING. feature_spec.json carries `scalingParams` — the actual FITTED params per tag (e.g. `{"TI-101": {"min": 70.0, "max": 75.0}}`), written by artifact_service.features() / feature_spec_service.py:241. ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey pins the exact spec (schema.prisma:1031), verified non-null on 73/73 runs. The primitive that applies a FITTED transform to new rows without re-fitting already exists and is tested: `to_model_ready(frame, tags, scalers, fitted_params=scaling_params)`, wrapped by `prepare_holdout_for_run`/`replay_holdout_for_run` (artifact_service.py:570-706), which already REFUSES when a tag would scale without a recorded scalingParams entry (artifact_service.py:676-687) rather than silently re-fitting. Serving's answer to 'call it or extract it' (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03's own question) is CALL IT — these entry points are object-storage-keyed (`store.get_frame(source_key)`), which fits MODEL-SERVE-006's parquet windows directly; a synchronous row-list /predict needs a thin in-memory wrapper, not an extraction. WHY THE ORIGINAL INFERENCE FAILED: the run examined had `target_scaled: false` and a 1.1 KiB model.joblib, read as 'no scalers at all'. Both premises are true and the conclusion is false — feature_spec_service.py:250 sets `target_scaled` from `scalers.get(target_y, "none")` (the TARGET defaults to none), while feature_service.py:79 sets `DEFAULT_SCALER = "minmax"` (FEATURES default to minmax). Two different defaults in one document. The joblib is small because scalers were never in the pickle — they live in the spec, not the model object. See the new empty-`scaling` finding below for the trap this created.

NEW 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03), HIGHEST-SEVERITY FINDING OF THIS AUDIT PASS — THE EMPTY-`scaling` TRAP. feature_service.py:79 sets `DEFAULT_SCALER = "minmax"`. feature_spec_service.py's `scaling` array (line ~23) holds one `{tag, method}` entry ONLY for a tag with an EXPLICIT scaler choice — a tag left at the default writes NOTHING to `scaling`, even though it IS scaled. Measured directly against all 21 `feature_spec.json` objects currently in MinIO: every single one has `len(scaling) == 0` while `len(scalingParams) == 22`. So on every real dataset in this system, every tag is minmax-scaled by default, and `scaling: []` is exactly what that looks like on disk — indistinguishable, by that field alone, from 'nothing was scaled'. A serving process that reads `scaling` to decide whether to transform inputs, finds it empty, and concludes no scaling is needed will feed RAW values into a model fitted on SCALED inputs and return a plausible wrong number — silently, with no error, no missing field, nothing to alert on. The existing preprocessing code is safe today only because `to_model_ready` reads `scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER)`, never `scaling` directly. Any new serving code (MODEL-SERVE-002-T05, MODEL-SERVE-006-T03) MUST resolve each tag's scaler the same way — from `scalingParams`' keys and/or the same default-aware lookup — never by branching on whether `scaling` is non-empty.

NEW 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T04) — SERVABILITY CENSUS AGAINST LIVE DATA. Read all 21 `feature_spec.json` objects in MinIO and cross-referenced against the live dev Postgres: 0 of 21 specs have a non-empty `derived_from_target` (the target-history request-contract fork in MODEL-SERVE-002-T06 guards a class the schema permits but no real spec currently uses); 0 of 21 have `target_scaled: true`; exactly 1 of 21 has zero `scalingParams` entries and is therefore UNSERVABLE without re-fitting — and it is `drafts/c47bfa69-.../artifacts/b9e25f8d-.../feature_spec.json`, the exact artifact this ledger's own MinIO screenshot and repeated findings are built from (it predates DS-LAKE-018-T02, so it has no recorded fitted params). The coverage guard in `prepare_holdout_for_run` (artifact_service.py:676-687) already refuses to serve it rather than silently re-fitting, which is the correct behaviour. Of 73 ModelTrainingRun rows, 0 have a null `featureSpecKey`, and 61 SUCCEEDED. This ledger's most-cited example run is its ONLY unservable one, which is worth knowing before anyone scopes MODEL-SERVE-002 against it as a representative case.

IMAGE_DIGEST CREATES A NEW RETENTION DEPENDENCY. Pinning by digest is the right call, but a digest pins nothing once the image is garbage-collected from the registry — at which point the ONLY record of the runtime a production model was fitted under is a string that resolves to nothing. Whatever retains the model object and its artifact must extend to the trainer image any live ModelVersion names. This dependency did not exist under the version-string approach this ledger originally proposed; it is a consequence of the better mechanism, not a defect in it.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T06). ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NEW — `drafts/` IS A SHARED ROOT FOR TWO UNRELATED ENTITIES IN ONE BUCKET. Observed directly: the run lives at drafts/1ce30923-…/runs/… (a ModelDraft) while its gold_object_key reads drafts/c47bfa69-…/artifacts/… (a DatasetDraft). Same bucket, same first segment, different tables, different lifecycles, different sweepers... The exposure is in the SWEEPERS... it is UNVERIFIED whether [DS-LAKE-014's DatasetDraft sweeper] reclaims by structural predicate or by a drafts/{id}/ prefix. If the latter, a dataset sweep can reach a model draft's prefix.' NOT REAL, confirmed by reading both call paths. MODEL-SERVE-002-V01 must select a non-CV (cvFoldsKey IS NULL) run specifically, not merely any SUCCEEDED run with scalingParams, or its own timestamp lookup silently fails to find a source row.

NEW 2026-09-02, DEV-ENVIRONMENT-ONLY, RECORDED BECAUSE IT COST REAL TIME TWICE — apps/python's presigned URLs default to S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT=http://host.docker.internal:9000, unresolvable when apps/serving runs directly on the host Mac (not in a container) during local live verification. Hit during both V01 and V04: each required restarting apps/python with S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9000 for the test, then restarting it back to normal afterward, PLUS restarting apps/serving fresh so its 30s descriptor-cache TTL wouldn't keep serving the stale (broken) presigned URL. Separately, a uvicorn --reload process survives a `pkill -f` pattern that omits the literal `--reload` substring (it breaks contiguous matching) — a stale, differently-cached process kept answering on the same port after an intended restart, which is what actually caused the first V04 attempt to look like a false pass. Not a code defect — both are pure dev-workflow hazards worth a line so the next person doesn't re-discover them: kill by exact PID (from `ps aux`), never by a pattern that might not match `--reload`'s insertion point; and any live test through apps/serving from the bare host needs the localhost override for the duration of the test only.

NEW 2026-09-02, LIVE-FOUND, FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE — apps/serving/services/loader.py's `_download` let a `requests` transport failure (e.g. unresolvable host, connection refused) propagate as a raw unhandled exception, reaching the /predict caller as an unmapped HTTP 500 with a leaked stack trace — found by chance when V04's first attempt hit an unresolvable host.docker.internal before the environment override was applied. This directly violated `LoadError`'s own docstring ('safe to surface as a 422, never a bare 500'). Fixed: `_download` now wraps `requests.RequestException` as `LoadError`, which `routers/serve.py` already mapped to 422 (a request-shaped 422 is used deliberately here, consistent with every other LoadError in this codepath, rather than introducing a separate 503-for-transient-failures distinction that no acceptance criterion asks for). Covered by a new unit test using a real unreachable port (127.0.0.1:1), not a mock.

NEW 2026-09-02, LIVE-FOUND — .github/workflows/_build-image.yml's `push:false` MODE WAS UNUSABLE UNTIL NOW, despite being declared in its own input schema (`push: {default: true}`). The 'Build and push' step never set `load:`, so with push:false the built image lands only in the buildx cache — nothing at `steps.ref.outputs.image` for the unconditional Trivy/SBOM steps below it to scan, which would fail on the very first push:false call. Never caught before because every existing caller (release.yml's 3 image jobs, all already broken/unwired for a different reason — the dslake-layout mismatch) uses the push:true default; MODEL-SERVE-002-T01's serving-image.yml is the first real push:false caller. Fixed with one line, `load: ${{ !inputs.push }}` — benefits any future build-and-scan-only caller of this shared workflow, not just serving.

PREMISE CORRECTION 2026-09-02 (MODEL-SERVE-002-T06) — THE SAMPLING-INTERVAL CLAUSE ASKS FOR AN AXIS THIS SYSTEM ALREADY DELIBERATELY REJECTED. T06's ORIGINAL text (2026-08-24, PRESERVED in its `detail`): 'Also validate the submitted history's sampling interval against the spec.' Three facts found by reading the tree, in the ledger's own tradition of each audit correcting its predecessor: (1) `feature_spec.json` RECORDS NO INTERVAL — read the whole of feature_spec_service.build_feature_spec: featureVersion, features, selectedColumns, scaling, scalingParams, encoding, featureHash, target_y, target_scaled, derived_from_target, and nothing else. Prisma has no interval column either (grepped schema.prisma). The interval exists only as a PI-fetch parameter (`summary_duration or '1m'`), never persisted with the artifact. So there is no reference value to validate anything against. (2) THIS REPO ALREADY FACED THE IDENTICAL QUESTION AND ANSWERED IT — artifact_service.py's holdout-replay lead-in check states it outright: 'Computed from the recipe's own compound lookback (max_replay_lookback — a lag on a rolling column compounds), NOT re-derived from a duration/interval a caller would have to look up.' It refuses in ROWS, from the recipe, precisely because an interval is the thing a caller would have to go look up. (3) The primitive already exists and is already proven: `max_replay_lookback`, written for DS-LAKE-018-T04, whose own docstring describes T06's exact failure mode ('null/wrong lag-rolling values ... feed straight into predict(), and depress the metric with no trace of why'). The clause's real defect is that it presumed a request contract that was never built: it assumed /predict would receive target history as a timestamped series, whereas the contract deliberately built passes PRE-COMPUTED feature columns and applies scaling only (the boundary recorded in this feature's own architecture note). Under that contract a lag column is an opaque number whose cadence is unknowable to serving — an interval check could only ever validate a caller's self-declaration, which is an attestation, not a proof. RESOLUTION, taken with the user: retire the interval clause and implement the row-depth guard the precedent already established — serving reports the recipe's compound row depth (via the same shared max_replay_lookback) in its refusal, so a caller learns how far back its history must reach. The alternative considered and rejected as its own future ticket: grow the contract to accept timestamped history and derive the target features in serving — which would require extracting apply_features into the shared package too, since deriving them with a second implementation is exactly the drift T05 exists to prevent. Worth stating plainly for whoever revisits: if that contract is ever built, the interval check becomes both possible AND meaningful, and this clause should be un-retired.

NEW 2026-09-02, LIVE-FOUND AND RESOLVED — TRIVY HARD GATE WOULD HAVE FAILED ON THE FIRST CI RUN. Scanned the real built apps/serving image locally with CI's exact parameters (severity HIGH,CRITICAL, ignore-unfixed) before trusting the workflow to it: 4 HIGH findings. Investigated each rather than blanket-suppressing: `msgpack` (GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964) and `setuptools` (CVE-2025-47273) are pip's OWN internal vendored copies (confirmed via `pip/_vendor/vendor.txt` inside the built image) — never imported by this repo's code, exercised only inside `pip install` itself, and unfixable from this side since pip 26.2.1 (the latest release at check time) still vendors these exact versions. `lightgbm` (CVE-2024-43598) and `pyarrow` (CVE-2026-25087) are both pinned specifically to match images/trainer/requirements.txt bit-for-bit (the entire reason for T01's separate-image requirement) — bumping either here alone would violate that pin and risk an unverified cross-version pickle roundtrip, a bigger risk than the CVEs' actual exposure (lightgbm's is an RCE via a malicious model file; every model this process loads is checksum-verified against a value read from Postgres, never attacker-supplied). All 4 recorded in .trivyignore with individual dated reasoning (msgpack/setuptools: 2027-03-01, lightgbm/pyarrow: 2026-12-01 — revisit even without an assigned owner). Re-scanned after: exit 0, confirmed live, not assumed.

CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (MODEL-SERVE-003 implementation start) — T04'S 'REUSE presign_artifact' IS RIGHT FOR THE INPUT, WRONG FOR THE OUTPUT. ORIGINAL, PRESERVED: 'Reuse the existing presign path (artifact_service.presign_artifact) rather than writing a second one.' ACTUALLY: presign_artifact (artifact_service.py:1322) refuses anything failing is_committed_artifact_key (object_store.py:1159), which requires BOTH '/artifacts/' in the key AND a filename in ALL_DATA_FILENAMES (:957). A prediction-job output key satisfies neither. The codebase forbids widening that guard in two places (artifact_service.py:1707-1710, schemas/preprocess.py:327-331) and records that this identical mistake already made holdoutMetrics null on 100% of runs — which is precisely why presign_run_object exists as a SECOND function (:1689), for run outputs that are real objects but not committed dataset artifacts either. A prediction-job output is the same shape of problem one level further out. Resolution: reuse presign_artifact to read the INPUT (an existing committed artifact, passes the guard unchanged); add a sibling function for the OUTPUT (prediction_job_key builder + is_prediction_job_key structural guard + presign_prediction_job_object), mirroring exactly how presign_run_object was added.

CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (MODEL-SERVE-003 implementation start) — T01'S VOCABULARY CLAIM IS RIGHT, AND STRONGER THAN STATED; ALSO, ModelFineTuningJob IS DEAD. ORIGINAL, PRESERVED: 'QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELED, mirroring ModelTrainingRun's vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one.' ACTUALLY: FOUR enums already carry this identical five-value set, not one — ModelRunStatus (schema.prisma:1000), PreprocessingJobStatus (:437), LoaderJobStatus (:445), ModelCandidateJobStatus (:1275). LoaderJobStatus's own doc comment states the reason to copy rather than share: 'mirrors PreprocessingJobStatus exactly, so the existing runner patterns (boot sweep, retry, attempt counting) transfer without inventing a second state machine.' PredictionJobStatus is the fifth copy, matching the house one-enum-per-entity convention — Prisma enums are not shared across models in this schema. Also found live: ModelFineTuningJob, which an earlier version of this ledger's own text referenced, no longer exists — it was renamed to ModelCandidateJob in migration 20260827120000_model_flow_013_candidate_job. Do not cite the old name in new work.

CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (MODEL-SERVE-003 implementation start) — T02'S IDEMPOTENCY CLAIM IS CONFIRMED GENUINELY NEW, AND SETTLES WHERE THE KEY LIVES. Searched the whole repo (idempotenc/Idempotency-Key/requestId/dedupe/dedup across apps/backend, apps/python, apps/frontend, apps/serving, packages/prisma): NO idempotency mechanism of any kind exists anywhere in this codebase today. Also checked: @Headers is used in ZERO non-spec backend files (grepped apps/backend/src) — the only inbound headers read anywhere in the backend are user-agent, in two auth controllers. So the idempotency key belongs in the submit endpoint's DTO BODY, not an HTTP header — introducing header-reading here would be the only instance of that pattern in the codebase, which is reason enough to avoid it absent a specific need. The race-safe shape to reuse already exists and is spec-tested, not merely a documented intention: dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts's resolveOrCreateEditDraftService — create, catch P2002 by CONSTRAINT NAME (model-version.authorized.service.ts:76-90's isUniqueViolation(err, constraint) pattern, 'checked by constraint name, not just P2002, so this never masks a genuinely different unique violation'), fall back to reading the winner's row. Tested at dataset-draft.authorized.service.spec.ts:2993 and :3018.

COMPLETED 2026-09-02 (MODEL-SERVE-003) — ALL 5 TASKS + 3 LIVE VERIFICATIONS DONE. Batch prediction ships as MODE=batch on the trainer image (soft-sensor-trainer 1.0.6 — bumped and default-tagged in trainning-container.authorized.service.ts, same discipline as every prior MODE addition: the default image MUST carry the new entrypoint or a job passes validation, spawns, and dies inside the container). images/trainer's own pytest suite (27/27) run for the first time this feature cycle and confirmed green before the image was rebuilt/retagged. Full round trip live-verified end-to-end against a real backend, real Postgres, real MinIO, and a real spawned container: submit -> claim -> chunked score -> upload -> complete -> presigned result, output byte-exact against a reference using the same softsensor_scaling.to_model_ready /predict itself calls. TWO REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION, not merely designed around: (1) the submit route was POST /predict:batch, which find-my-way (Fastify's router) parses as a param opener rather than a literal colon — it happened to match the literal string but ALSO matched any /predict<suffix>; fixed to /predict-batch. (2) this file's isUniqueViolation (and, discovered but NOT fixed here, its identical copies in model-version.authorized.service.ts and dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts) checked err.meta.target for the P2002 constraint name, but this Prisma version's driver-adapter error shape has no `target` field at all — reproduced live, the constraint name only appears inside meta.driverAdapterError.cause.originalMessage. The 'catch P2002 by constraint name, fall back to the winner's row' pattern this ledger has cited as proven-safe in three places was, in practice, dead code on every one of the OTHER two call sites: a genuine race there currently surfaces a raw 500 instead of the intended graceful fallback / clean 409. Fixed here; flagged as an open follow-up for the other two files, which this feature's scope does not cover. All infra used for live verification (seeded Model/ModelVersion rows, uploaded synthetic SILVER inputs, spawned containers, prediction output objects) was cleaned up after each check — nothing left seeded in the dev database or MinIO.

tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: no longer 'trace the whole preprocessing path' — feature_columns is inlined in run_manifest.json, so column selection and order are already recoverable. Scope narrows to scalers alone. CHOOSE THE RUN DELIBERATELY: the observed OLS run has no scalers (target_scaled: false, and a 1.1 KiB model.joblib consistent with a bare estimator), so it cannot answer the question no matter how carefully it is read. tasks.detail: apps/python artifact_service.py (select_columns, force_keep_target, the scalers path) and feature_spec_service.py. Answer one question: can a serving process apply the identical transform to raw input by calling the same code, or does something in that path assume a whole parquet frame rather than a handful of rows? The answer decides whether serving is a thin loader or needs an extracted, shared transform module — a difference in kind, not degree. Do NOT plan to reimplement it either way; see the findings.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: PREMISE INVERTED (per findings[]): scaler state is NOT missing. feature_spec.json's `scalingParams` carries the fitted params, ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey pins the exact spec (verified non-null on 73/73 runs), and `to_model_ready(..., fitted_params=scaling_params)` already applies a fitted transform without re-fitting, with an existing refuse-rather-than-silently-re-fit guard. ANSWER: call it, not extract it — the existing entry points are object-storage-keyed, which fits MODEL-SERVE-006 directly; a synchronous /predict needs a thin in-memory wrapper. Also surfaced the empty-`scaling`-array trap (new finding) — the real risk in this area, and the opposite of what this task originally worried about.

tasks.title: Establish what retains the fitted artifact, and pin it if nothing does
tasks.detail:
OPENED 2026-08-24 from the observation that feature_spec.json is not in the run directory. Read DatasetArtifact's lifecycle: is there any path — a dataset edit, a version supersession, MODEL-FLOW-011's sweep, an admin delete — that can remove or orphan an artifact a ModelTrainingRun points at? Check the artifact's own retention alongside the draft-prefix question MODEL-SERVE-000-T06 asks; they are two objects with one consequence and it is cheaper to answer them in one read.

IF NOTHING RETAINS IT: the fix is upstream at Save Model, not here — MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 should record the artifact id and featureSpecKey on the saved Model so the reference is explicit and greppable, and whatever guards artifact deletion must treat a referencing ModelVersion the way MODEL-FLOW-011-T05 treats an adopted run. Deliverable of THIS task is the finding plus the upstream ticket, not a guard written in the wrong ledger.

DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY COPYING feature_spec.json INTO THE RUN PREFIX. That trades a reference problem for a divergence problem and contradicts the adopt-by-pointer rule MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 states, for the same reason it states it.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: CORRECTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (see findings[]). Pinning already exists on ModelTrainingRun (goldArtifactId/goldObjectKey/artifactChecksum/featureSpecKey). Protection already exists: measured live, 100% of 73 runs (0 GOLD) train against FINAL, which is unconditionally excluded from the cleanup candidate query and predicate. 0 of 61 SUCCEEDED runs point at a missing or reclaimed artifact. Both named as upstream tickets (MODEL-FLOW/DS-LAKE), not written here. Also opened decisions.open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_bytes for MODEL-SERVE-001 to resolve.

features.title: Model Version Registry — One Row Decides What Is In Production
features.description: Give a Model a versioned, staged history so that promotion and rollback are row changes. Nothing here serves anything; this is the pointer everything downstream reads.

tasks.title: ModelVersion entity
tasks.detail: Shape depends on MODEL-SERVE-000-T02. Fields: modelId, version, the artifact pointer and checksum, feature spec reference, framework + version, sourceRunId, sourceDatasetId, metrics, stage, timestamps, promotedById. A version row is IMMUTABLE except for stage — same discipline as MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's adopt-by-pointer: the row records what happened, it is not a workspace.
tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: the artifact reference is NOT optional and NOT derivable later. Because the run directory holds no feature spec (see findings), ModelVersion must record the fitted DatasetArtifact's id and its featureSpecKey explicitly, alongside the model object pointer. Resolving it at serve time by walking to the dataset's CURRENT artifact would be silently wrong for any model whose dataset was edited after training — and it would be wrong in the direction that still returns a number.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: MODEL-SERVE-000 confirmed the run row already stores exactly this (ModelTrainingRun.goldArtifactId/goldObjectKey/artifactChecksum/featureSpecKey, verified non-null on 73/73 runs) — this task copies those four fields onto ModelVersion at promotion-worthy points, it does not invent them. Also: decisions.open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_bytes is now open and must be resolved as part of this task — does ModelVersion reference the source artifact by pointer (per MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's adopt-by-pointer rule) or copy its bytes into a version-owned prefix (per DS-LAKE-025's adopt_artifact precedent)? Record the choice in that decision with its rejected alternative.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. `ModelVersion` model + `ModelVersionStage` enum added to schema.prisma (migration 20260901090000_model_serve_001_model_version), migrated and verified against the live dev DB. decisions.open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_bytes resolved POINTER with rejected alternative recorded (see that decision). FOUND AND FIXED DURING IMPLEMENTATION, NOT PART OF THE ORIGINAL SPEC: (1) the migration's `ModelVersion_sourceRunId_fkey` was originally `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — verified live (rolled-back transaction, then a real cascade-delete of a seeded Model+run+version) that this breaks `deleteModelService` (`model.authorized.service.ts`'s bare `prisma.model.delete`), because a Model delete cascades onto BOTH ModelTrainingRun and ModelVersion in one statement and RESTRICT is checked immediately per-row rather than deferred to end-of-statement. Changed to `NO ACTION` in both the migration and schema.prisma, migration dropped and cleanly reapplied (table was empty, zero data loss) since it had already been applied by an earlier session with the broken FK. Re-verified live: a real `DELETE FROM "Model"` with a full Model+run+version chain now cascades cleanly. (2) `model_sha256` — needed for `ModelVersion.modelChecksum` — was NOT actually a `ModelTrainingRun` column despite three docstrings (RunManifestRequest, RunManifestResponse's router description, get_run_manifest) all claiming it was; verified against schema.prisma and fixed at the source: `get_run_manifest`/`RunManifestResponse` now read and return it from run_manifest.json (same honest-legacy-null policy as framework_versions), all three stale docstrings corrected in place. Live-verified against a real run's manifest: `model_sha256` now returns `'b5d52d61150a161...117065'` where it previously silently returned nothing. Save Model (T03) now populates version 1's `modelChecksum` from this.

tasks.title: Stage machine and the single-production constraint
tasks.detail: STAGING -> PRODUCTION -> ARCHIVED. Enforce at most one PRODUCTION per modelId AT THE DATABASE, with a partial unique index, not in service code. Application-level uniqueness under concurrent promotes is the same class of hole MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's 409 guard closes for double-save, and the same reason MODEL-FLOW-002-T07 used a CHECK constraint rather than a service check.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. `ModelVersion_one_production_per_model`, a partial unique index (`ON ("modelId") WHERE stage = 'PRODUCTION'`), same hand-written-migration precedent as `ModelFineTuningJob_one_live_per_draft` — Prisma's schema DSL cannot express a partial index. The pure stage-transition predicate lives at `apps/backend/src/lib/model-version-transitions.ts` (`isPromotable`), mirroring `dataset-version-transitions.ts`'s shape but a DIFFERENT graph: ARCHIVED -> PRODUCTION is legal here (a rollback is a promote), which the dataset side's strict forward line does not allow — documented in that file's own doc comment. Live-proven under real concurrency in V01 (see verification).

tasks.title: Save Model creates version 1 in STAGING, never PRODUCTION
tasks.detail: Saving is not deploying. A wizard whose last click puts a model in front of live traffic has no step at which someone decides it should be. This is additive to MODEL-FLOW-007-T04's transaction, inside the same transaction — a Model with no version row is a state nothing downstream can interpret.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. `ModelDraftAuthorizedService.saveDraftService` (model-draft.authorized.service.ts) now creates `ModelVersion` version 1 inside the SAME `$transaction` as the `Model` create and the `ModelTrainingRun`/`ModelDraft` updates — no separate write, no window where a Model can exist without a version row. `version: 1` is hardcoded (not max()+1: `created` is a brand-new Model in this same transaction, so no other version can exist yet — a future retrain minting a later version needs DS-LAKE-009-T03's max()+1 allocation, this path does not). `stage` is never set on create, so it takes the schema's `STAGING` default — verified live via V01's seed rows (queried back as STAGING before any promote). Fields are copied one-hop from the adopted `ModelTrainingRun` row's own pinned columns, never re-derived through the dataset's current artifact.

tasks.title: Promote and rollback endpoints
tasks.detail: POST .../versions/:v/promote and POST .../rollback, both recording who and when. Rollback is promote pointed at the previous PRODUCTION — not a distinct mechanism, so it cannot rot separately. Envelope per the findings.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. New module `apps/backend/src/api/v1/model-version/` (mirroring the model-run/model-draft/model-draft-cleanup convention of one module per feature despite tight coupling to Model), registered in `app.module.ts`. `POST authorized/model/:modelId/versions/:version/promote` (`:version` is the integer version number, not the row id — a human-operable natural key given `@@unique([modelId, version])`) and `POST authorized/model/:modelId/rollback`. Both funnel through one private `promote()` method — rollback resolves the most-recently-`archivedAt` ARCHIVED row and calls the SAME gate (T05 object check, T06 r2 floor), per the feature's own 'not a distinct mechanism' decision. Both record `promotedById`/`promotedAt`. Standard `{statusCode, message, type, data}` envelope, editor-level access (`assertModelAccess`, same rule as every other mutating Model route). An already-PRODUCTION promote is an idempotent no-op, matching `isLegalTransition`'s own documented policy split on the dataset side. TIGHTENED DURING ADVISORY REVIEW: rollback's lookup originally read `where: { stage: 'ARCHIVED', archivedAt: { not: null } }` — correct only BY ABSENCE, since only `promote()` writes ARCHIVED today, not by construction. Added `promotedAt: { not: null }` (set only by `promote()`'s own transaction) so a version that reaches ARCHIVED through some future path without ever having been PRODUCTION cannot become a rollback target. Also: the override's `actorName` was `user.email` — changed to the same firstName/lastName-then-fallback resolution `updateModelService`'s `editorName` already uses, so a promotion override records the same identity string as the rest of the Model audit trail rather than a login email.

tasks.title: Refuse to promote a version whose artifact cannot be loaded
tasks.detail: Verify object existence and checksum BEFORE flipping the stage. A promote that succeeds against a missing or altered object turns a deploy into an outage discovered by the first request, and the rollback path is then also untested. This is the one place a slow check is worth it.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. No existing primitive covered this — `/artifacts/presign` is hard-restricted to committed dataset artifacts (`is_committed_artifact_key`) and refuses `model.joblib` outright, so a new endpoint was added rather than reusing it: `POST /v1/preprocess/models/runs/verify-object` (`artifact_service.verify_model_object`, guarded by the same `is_draft_run_key`/`is_model_run_key` structural check `run_predictions`/`get_run_manifest` already use) returns `{exists, checksum}`, checksum computed from the object's own bytes via `store.checksum_of`. Backend wrapper `verifyModelObject` in `python-preprocess-client.ts`. `promote()` calls it BEFORE the transaction: refuses (422) if `!exists` unconditionally, and refuses (422) on a checksum mismatch ONLY when `ModelVersion.modelChecksum` is non-null. NAMED EXPLICITLY, NOT LEFT IMPLICIT (flagged in advisory review): `modelChecksum` is null for any version whose source run predates the manifest recording `model_sha256` — MODEL-SERVE-000-T04's own servability census found the ledger's own most-cited example run is exactly this shape — so for those versions the checksum half of this task's acceptance criterion does not apply; only existence is checked. This is the same honest-legacy-null policy `frameworkVersions` already established, not a gap introduced here, but the acceptance criterion 'promoting a version whose checksum does not match fails' holds unconditionally only for versions created after this change (i.e. every version going forward, since T01 now populates `modelChecksum` on every save whose manifest has it). LIVE-VERIFIED end to end against real MinIO (not mocked) for the primitive itself: wrote a real object, confirmed `exists:true` + a real sha256 checksum, deleted it, confirmed `exists:false, checksum:null`, and confirmed the structural guard refuses a non-run-shaped key (e.g. a dataset artifact path) by name rather than silently accepting it. See V02.

tasks.title: Refuse to promote a version whose metrics fail a floor, unless overridden on the record
tasks.detail:
OPENED 2026-08-24 after observing r2 = -2.4068 on a run this project's own live verification recorded as successful. A negative R² is not a marginal model, it is a model with no predictive value, and there is currently no boundary at which anyone is asked whether it should go to production.

The floor must be a REFUSAL, not a warning. A warning at promote time is read once by the person who already decided to promote, which is the moment it has least effect. Make r2 <= 0 a hard block; anything above that is a judgement call and belongs to the human, not to a threshold this task invents.

An override must be possible — a deliberately weak model has legitimate uses (a baseline to beat, a smoke test of the serving path) — but it must be RECORDED on the ModelVersion with an actor and a reason, so that 'why is this in production' has an answer six months later. An override that leaves no trace is the same as no floor.

DO NOT PUT THIS IN THE WIZARD INSTEAD. Step 4 Evaluation showing a negative R² prominently is good and separate; MODEL-FLOW-004 owns it. The promote boundary needs its own gate because promotion is reachable without the wizard — see MODEL-SERVE-001-T04's endpoints.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED, WITH TWO GAPS THE TICKET DID NOT SPELL OUT MADE EXPLICIT DURING IMPLEMENTATION (per this feature's own advisory review): (1) an UNREADABLE r2 (no `metrics`, or `metrics.r2` not a finite number — `extractR2`, mirroring `extractRmse`'s existing narrowing convention in model-candidate-job.authorized.service.ts) is treated the SAME as a failing score, never as a silent pass — an unknown r2 is not evidence the model is good. (2) `PromoteOverrideSchema.reason` is `z.string().trim().min(1)` — REQUIRED and non-empty, enforced at the DTO boundary, not just documented as should-be-required. `promotionOverride` is `{actorId, actorName, reason, at}`, written only on the ARCHIVED->skip path (never when r2 > 0), and is part of the same atomic promote transaction so an override is never recorded without the promote it justifies actually taking effect.

tasks.title: Retain the trainer image digest a live version names
tasks.detail: OPENED 2026-08-24. run_manifest.json pins provenance by image_digest, which is the strongest form available — and worthless once that image leaves the registry. Establish whether the registry has any GC or tag-expiry policy, and if so, exclude digests named by a non-ARCHIVED ModelVersion. This is the same class of problem as MODEL-FLOW-011-T05 and MODEL-SERVE-000-T07: a reference held in one system to an object another system is free to delete. Third instance of the pattern in this project, which is the argument for stating it as a rule rather than fixing it three times.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED AS DOCUMENTATION, PER THE TASK'S OWN SHAPE — this is an audit-and-record task, not a build task. CORRECTED DURING ADVISORY REVIEW: an earlier draft of this result claimed no `.github/workflows` directory exists, which is false — verified live: `.github/workflows/` holds `ci.yml`, `release.yml`, `_build-image.yml`, `_deploy.yml`, `security.yml`. Grepped all five for `retention|expire|gc|prune|cleanup|delete`: the only hits are `actions/upload-artifact`'s `retention-days: 7` (CI test-log artifacts) in ci.yml — unrelated to container registry images. So the CONCLUSION stands (no image garbage collection runs today) but the evidence is now the actual grep, not an absent-directory claim that was never checked. `ModelVersion.imageDigest` already retains exactly the fact a future GC policy would need to consult (a non-ARCHIVED ModelVersion's digest must be excluded from deletion) — this task's deliverable, per its own wording, is establishing that fact and recording the rule, not building a GC exclusion for a GC process that does not exist. RULE RECORDED (fourth instance of the pattern the task itself calls out as recurring — MODEL-FLOW-011-T05, MODEL-SERVE-000-T07's two exposures, and this one): if a registry GC/retention workflow is ever added to this repo, it MUST query `ModelVersion` for `imageDigest` values where `stage != 'ARCHIVED'` (STAGING and PRODUCTION both — a staged-but-not-yet-promoted version's digest must survive too) and exclude those digests, the same way `artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts`'s cleanup query already excludes FINAL-type artifacts unconditionally.

acceptance_criteria: Save Model produces exactly one ModelVersion at STAGING and no PRODUCTION version.
Two concurrent promotes against one model cannot both leave a PRODUCTION row — enforced by the database, proven by a concurrent test rather than by reading the service.
Rollback restores the previous PRODUCTION version and is recorded with an actor.
Promoting a version whose object is missing or whose checksum does not match fails and leaves the current PRODUCTION untouched.
A ModelVersion row's artifact pointer, checksum and metrics are never updated after creation.

verification.description: Fire two promotes concurrently against different versions of one model and confirm exactly one PRODUCTION row survives. Sequential promotes would pass a weaker test while leaving the race entirely uncovered — the constraint this feature adds exists for the concurrent case.
verification.result_2026_09_01: LIVE-PROVEN against the real dev DB, at the SQL level rather than through the NestJS/auth stack (no backend server was running to exercise HTTP end to end; the actual mechanism under test — the partial unique index — is a DB-level guarantee, so a real concurrent DB test proves the acceptance criterion directly). Seeded one Model with two STAGING ModelVersions under two real ModelTrainingRun rows. Two concurrent `psql` sessions each opened a transaction and updated a DIFFERENT version to `stage='PRODUCTION'`, staggered so both UPDATEs landed before either committed. Observed: transaction A's UPDATE succeeded and committed; transaction B's UPDATE BLOCKED (Postgres's standard behavior for a value that might conflict with an uncommitted row), then on A's commit failed immediately with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "ModelVersion_one_production_per_model"` and rolled back. Final state queried: exactly one PRODUCTION row (version-1), version-2 untouched at STAGING. This is precisely the P2002-on-that-constraint-name path `ModelVersionAuthorizedService`'s `promote()` catches and maps to a 409. Test rows cleaned up via `DELETE FROM "Model"` (cascades) — which also re-confirmed T01's FK fix live a second time.

verification.description: Delete the object behind a STAGING version, attempt to promote it, and confirm both the refusal AND that the previously live version is still PRODUCTION and still loadable.
verification.result_2026_09_01: LIVE-PROVEN at the Python primitive level against real MinIO (same scoping note as V01 — no backend/python server was running for a full HTTP round trip; the novel mechanism, `verify_model_object`, was exercised directly and for real, not mocked). Wrote a real object to a synthetic run-shaped key, called `verify_model_object` and got `{exists: true, checksum: <real sha256>}`; deleted the object; called it again and got `{exists: false, checksum: null}`. Also confirmed the structural guard refuses a non-run-shaped key (a dataset-artifact path) by name. The TS-side refusal (`promote()` throwing 422 on `!verified.exists` BEFORE the `$transaction` that would flip stage even opens) was verified by type-check and code review rather than a second live HTTP call: since the throw happens before any DB write, 'the previously-live version is still PRODUCTION and still loadable' follows by construction — there is no code path where a failed T05 check reaches the transaction.

verification.description: Complete Save Model and assert zero PRODUCTION rows exist for that model. The mirror of MODEL-FLOW-007-V01, one boundary later.
verification.result_2026_09_01: VERIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION PLUS A LIVE DEFAULT CHECK, not a full wizard run (no backend server was running this session). `saveDraftService`'s new `tx.modelVersion.create` call never sets `stage`, so the column takes the schema's `@default(STAGING)` — confirmed live via V01's seeded rows, which likewise never set `stage` explicitly and read back as `STAGING` before any promote touched them. Since STAGING is the only value the create path can produce and PRODUCTION is reachable only through `promote()` (a separate, later call), zero PRODUCTION rows can exist for a model immediately after Save Model, for the same structural reason MODEL-FLOW-007-V01 established for the Model row itself.

tasks.title: Serving image, without the trainer's fit-time dependencies
tasks.detail: Note the deployment-currency trap MODEL-FLOW-000-T04's verification_note already recorded for the trainer: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile, so repo source being correct proves nothing about what is deployed. Do not inherit that. The serving image gets a CI build from the first commit, or it acquires the same untraceable drift.
tasks.result_2026_09_02: apps/serving/Dockerfile (python:3.12-slim, non-root uid 10001, libgomp1 for lightgbm/xgboost) built and LIVE-VERIFIED locally, not just written: `docker build` succeeded, the editable packages/py-scaling install resolved correctly (confirms the monorepo-relative WORKSPACE layout choice was right — build context is repo root since py-scaling lives outside apps/serving), and a running container answered /healthz and /readyz correctly with the backend unreachable, matching T03's own design. tasks.title: Multi-model loader with a bounded cache
tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: verify model_sha256 (the field name is now known, not hypothesised) and verify image_digest against the serving runtime — noting that a digest match is not achievable if serving runs a DIFFERENT image from the trainer, which decisions.training_and_serving_are_separate_planes deliberately requires. So the digest is a provenance record to CHECK FOR PRESENCE and log, not a value to match. What must actually be validated at load is that the serving runtime's own library versions are compatible with the pickle; the digest tells you what to go and look up when they are not.
tasks.detail: Resolve model_id -> PRODUCTION version -> object; verify checksum; verify the recorded framework version against the runtime and REFUSE on a mismatch rather than warn (see findings — a silently-loaded mismatch produces plausible wrong numbers). Cache bounded by memory, not by entry count: models differ in size by orders of magnitude and a count-based cap sizes for the smallest one.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: MODEL-SERVE-000 found the loader must also resolve scaler state alongside the model object — read feature_spec.json's scalingParams via ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey (one hop, verified non-null on 73/73 runs) at the same load step, and resolve each tag's method the way to_model_ready does (scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER)), never by checking whether the spec's `scaling` array is non-empty — see the empty-`scaling`-array trap finding, which is real and specific to this task.
tasks.result_2026_09_02: apps/backend GET /authorized/serving/models/:modelId/descriptor (new model-serving module, ServingTokenGuard shared-secret auth) resolves PRODUCTION version -> presigned model URL + checksum + featureColumns (from run_manifest.json) + scalers/scalingParams (from feature_spec.json, resolved via scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER) per the empty-scaling-array finding, never by branching on scaling's emptiness) + frameworkVersions + imageDigest. apps/serving/services/loader.py (ModelLoader) downloads -> sha256-verifies (refuses on mismatch, honest-legacy-null on absent) -> checks frameworkVersions against the runtime (refuses on mismatch, warns on absent) -> joblib.load, in a bytes-bounded LRU keyed by (modelId, versionId). Live-verified: V01 (correct load + correct predict) and V04 (tampered checksum genuinely refused with both hashes named in the error) both ran against real Postgres + MinIO + a real fitted model, not synthetic fixtures. A real gap was found and fixed along the way: a network failure during download reached the caller as an unhandled 500 (violating LoadError's own stated invariant) — _download now wraps requests.RequestException as LoadError, unit-tested via a real unreachable-port connection failure.

tasks.title: Warm the production set before reporting ready
tasks.detail: /healthz answers without touching MinIO or Postgres (a liveness probe that depends on them turns a dependency blip into a restart loop); /readyz answers only after the production set is loaded. Getting this backwards means traffic arrives during cold load and the first caller pays for everyone.
tasks.result_2026_09_02: main.py's lifespan warms every model from GET /authorized/serving/production-versions on boot (each individual warm failure logged, never fatal) and app.state.ready flips true once the pass completes regardless of outcome. /healthz is static, touches nothing. /readyz is 503 while not ready, 200 after. Unit-tested including backend-unreachable-at-boot (readyz still reaches ready). Not yet live-verified against a real production set with more than one model.

Reject with a message naming the offending column. sklearn's own error on a mismatched frame names a column and explains nothing — the same complaint MODEL-FLOW-010-T07 makes about pyarrow's 'No match for FieldRef.Name' reaching a user who cannot act on it. The range checks the dataset wizard's feature presets already express are the natural source for a range warning here; reuse rather than restate.

tasks.detail: Per MODEL-SERVE-000-T03's answer. If the path is callable, call it. If it is not, extract it into a module BOTH the trainer and the server import, and make the trainer use the extracted copy in the same change — leaving the trainer on the original and the server on a copy is precisely the drift this task exists to prevent, and it would pass every test written against either side alone.

Also validate the submitted history's sampling interval against the spec. A model in this class served without history does not error — it predicts from imputed or absent lags and returns a number, which is the failure mode with no symptom.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: Measured: 0 of 21 live feature_spec.json objects have a non-empty derived_from_target. This guard governs a class the schema permits but no real model in this system currently belongs to — keep the guard (schema allows it), but do not treat /predict's request-contract fork as validated against real data; it is untested against a real target-derived model because none exists yet.
tasks.status_2026_09_02: SUPERSEDED, PRESERVED: 'PARTIAL, AND THE REMAINDER IS BLOCKED, NOT MERELY UNBUILT. ... The sampling-interval half of this task's own detail line CANNOT be built against the current request contract ... BLOCKED: what's needed is a decision on the request contract shape for target-derived models, not implementation effort.' That framing was half right — the interval cannot be validated against this contract — but it missed that THIS REPO HAD ALREADY DECIDED THE INTERVAL IS THE WRONG AXIS. What was built: (1) `max_replay_lookback` (with `feature_column_name`/`_reads_tags`/`_own_lookback`) moved out of apps/python into softsensor_scaling.features — the same extract-and-switch-the-caller-in-one-change pattern T05 used; apps/python imports them back under their original names, so artifact_service.py:95/533 and tests/test_feature_spec_quirks.py are untouched, and apps/python's full suite stayed green with only its 3 known pre-existing failures. tasks.title: Invalidate the cache on promote
tasks.result_2026_09_02: Contract chosen, implemented, and LIVE-PROVEN under continuous load (V02: 90/90 requests succeeded, switchover at t=30.44s against a promote at t=5.25s, both consistent with the 30s TTL). services/descriptor.py caches descriptors with a 30s TTL (decisions.serving_cache_staleness_bound) and offers invalidate(); services/loader.py's ModelLoader.invalidate() exists but nothing calls it on a promote webhook yet — the bound today is TTL-driven only, never sooner than the TTL. Remaining work, if the bound is ever tightened below 30s: wire a promote-triggered invalidate() call (webhook or poll) instead of relying on TTL expiry alone.
tasks.detail: After a promote, replicas holding the old version keep serving it until something tells them. Whatever the mechanism (a short TTL on the version lookup is the cheapest and is probably enough), the CONTRACT is what matters: state the maximum time a promoted version can take to become live, and make it a number someone chose rather than an emergent property. Silent divergence between two replicas answering the same request differently is very hard to diagnose from the outside.

acceptance_criteria: A promoted model answers /predict with no image rebuild and no redeploy.
A request missing a required column is refused with that column named — not a 500 from the estimator.
A model whose feature spec is target-derived cannot be served without target history, and the refusal states why.
The transform applied at inference is the SAME CODE as the one applied at training, not an equivalent one.
A checksum or framework-version mismatch prevents a load; it never degrades to a warning.
/healthz does not depend on MinIO or Postgres; /readyz does.
After a promote, every replica serves the new version within the stated bound.

verification.description: Load a model whose feature spec declares a non-empty derived_from_target and confirm a history-less request is refused. Then submit history at the WRONG sampling interval and confirm it is also refused — a serving process that accepts the second has not implemented this task, only half of it.
verification.note_2026_09_02: SUPERSEDED, PRESERVED: 'HALF DONE, HALF BLOCKED (not merely unrun) ... Wrong-sampling-interval: CANNOT run — the check itself cannot be built without first deciding the request contract for target-derived models. Decision needed: should /predict accept a timestamped history sequence for target-derived models (a request-shape change), or is presence-only sufficient given zero real models in this class today?'
verification.result_2026_09_02: COMPLETED against a fabricated target-derived fixture, as this verification's own text anticipates it must be (0 of 21 live specs have derived_from_target). The fixture is the COMPOUNDING case on purpose — 'lag 3 of the target, then a rolling(12) mean of that lag' — whose true depth is 15, a number a non-compounding implementation would silently under-report as 12; that is asserted directly. Proven: (a) a history-less request is refused, with the message naming both the missing column and the 15-observation depth; (b) a request carrying the full history columns is accepted; (c) a BATCH where only one row omits the column is still refused (one good row does not excuse another that would predict from an absent lag); (d) a descriptor with no recipe reports depth 0 and omits the depth sentence rather than fabricating one; (e) an unreadable recipe does not turn a satisfiable request into a 500. The second half of this verification's original text — 'submit history at the WRONG sampling interval and confirm it is also refused' — is RETIRED, not skipped, and not silently dropped: see the premise-correction finding dated 2026-09-02. In short, the interval is not the axis this system validates on; the recipe's compound ROW depth is, and that is what both this guard and prepare_holdout_for_run now refuse on, via one shared function.
