features.title: Batch Prediction and Job Results
features.description: Score a parquet input in object storage as an asynchronous job, and return the result by reference. This is the '/predict + /result' pair from the original question, split because they are two different operations.

tasks.title: PredictionJob entity and its state machine
tasks.detail: QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELED, mirroring ModelTrainingRun's vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one. State in Postgres, never in process memory — MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's stranded run is the demonstration of what in-memory job tracking does across a restart, and a result endpoint answering 404 for a job that finished is the same bug with a friendlier face. RESULT 2026-09-02: PredictionJob + PredictionJobStatus (fifth copy of the 5-value vocabulary) added to schema.prisma, hand-written migration for the partial unique index (modelId, idempotencyKey) WHERE idempotencyKey IS NOT NULL. Applied via db:migrate:deploy, table confirmed live via psql.

tasks.title: POST /predict:batch with an idempotency key
tasks.detail: Returns a job id immediately. The idempotency key is not optional: MODEL-FLOW-003-T09 had to add poll-failure tolerance specifically because a transient error pushed users toward a retry that would spawn a SECOND container against the same draft. A batch endpoint without a key has the identical hole and the same trigger. RESULT 2026-09-02: idempotencyKey in the DTO body (not a header — zero precedent for @Headers in this codebase). Submit: create -> P2002 caught by constraint name -> fall back to reading the winner's row. LIVE-VERIFIED under genuine concurrent submission (V02) after fixing a real bug found in that same test — see the P2002-shape finding below.

tasks.title: Batch worker, chunked
tasks.detail: Stream the input rather than loading it whole. MODEL-FLOW-010-V03 exists because a single unbounded read at 8,000 tags produced 76MB where 489KB was needed; a batch scorer is the most likely place for that to reappear, and it will reappear on someone else's data, not in a test. RESULT 2026-09-02: images/trainer/app/pipelines/batch.py streams the input via pq.ParquetFile(...).iter_batches(batch_size=50_000, columns=feature_columns) + incremental pq.ParquetWriter, mirroring export_service.py's BATCH_ROWS precedent. LIVE-VERIFIED twice: (1) in-container smoke test, 130K vs 1.5M rows, peak RSS 220.6MB -> 244.2MB despite 11.5x more data; (2) real end-to-end run through the actual backend+container+MinIO with an 8M-row / 1.19GB input (V01's job) completed successfully, confirming the bound holds against real infra, not just the in-container harness.

tasks.title: GET /jobs/:id — status, and the output by presigned reference
tasks.detail: Never stream result bytes through the API. Reuse the existing presign path (artifact_service.presign_artifact) rather than writing a second one, and honour MODEL-FLOW-000-T06's rule: neither the presign request nor the URL reaches a log, because the URL IS the capability. RESULT 2026-09-02: Input reuses presign_artifact unchanged (is_committed_artifact_key). Output is a SIBLING function, presign_prediction_job_object (+ presign_prediction_job_upload for the container's own writes) — never a widened is_committed_artifact_key guard, matching presign_run_object's own precedent and stated reason. GET /prediction-jobs/:jobId mints the output URL fresh on read. LIVE-VERIFIED end-to-end: real presigned GET URL returned by a real backend, real object downloaded from real MinIO, byte-exact against a reference computed with the same softsensor_scaling.to_model_ready call /predict uses (max abs diff 0.0 across 12 rows). ALSO FOUND AND FIXED: the route was originally POST /predict:batch, not /predict-batch — find-my-way (Fastify's router) parses a bare ':' as a param opener, so that path silently matched ANY /predict<suffix>, not just the literal string. Confirmed live against find-my-way@9.6.0 before switching to /predict-batch — see prediction-job.authorized.controller.ts's own comment.

tasks.title: Record which version scored the batch
tasks.detail: Pin the version at job START and store it on the job. A long batch spanning a promote must not silently score its first half on one model and its second on another — and a result whose model is 'whatever was production at some point' cannot be reproduced or defended later. RESULT 2026-09-02: modelVersionId pinned at submitPredictionJobService, never re-resolved. ModelServingAuthorizedService gained getDescriptorByVersionIdService (resolves ANY ModelVersion by id, no stage filter) alongside the existing getDescriptorService (current-PRODUCTION only) so claimJobService always reads the version pinned at submit, even after it is demoted. LIVE-VERIFIED as V03 below — an ARCHIVED version resolved correctly mid-job.

acceptance_criteria: The batch endpoint returns a job id without waiting for the work.
Job state survives a restart of the process that created it.
Results are delivered by presigned reference; no result bytes traverse the API.
The same idempotency key cannot produce two jobs.
Every job records the exact model version that scored it, pinned at start.
A batch over a wide input keeps memory bounded — no unbounded read of the input frame.

verification.description: Submit a batch, restart the serving process mid-flight, and confirm GET /jobs/:id still reports truthfully — either a completed job or a job that reached a terminal FAILED with a stated reason. Permanently RUNNING is the failure this checks for, and it is the exact state MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 observed on the training side. RESULT 2026-09-02, LIVE: submitted an 8M-row/1.19GB batch against a real backend, paused its container via `docker pause` right after spawn (containerId set, status RUNNING) to force a genuine in-flight window, then force-killed and restarted the backend process. Boot log: 'Reconciled 1 orphaned run/container(s) at boot' — the job stayed RUNNING (re-attached via container.inspect() + watch(), not marked FAILED for a container that still existed). Unpaused; the NEW process's re-attached watch() tracked it to real completion (SUCCEEDED, 8,000,000 rows) roughly 55s later. Never permanently RUNNING, never falsely FAILED for a live container.

Submit the same idempotency key twice concurrently and confirm one job. Sequential submission is a weaker test that a naive check would also pass. RESULT 2026-09-02, LIVE: fired two concurrent POST /predict-batch requests with the same idempotencyKey (bash background jobs, same instant). FIRST ATTEMPT FOUND A REAL BUG: both this file's isUniqueViolation and its two precedents (model-version.authorized.service.ts, dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts) check err.meta.target, which does not exist on this Prisma version's driver-adapter P2002 shape — reproduced live, the actual meta was {modelName, driverAdapterError:{cause:{originalCode:'23505', originalMessage:'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "PredictionJob_idempotency_key"', constraint:{fields:[...]}}}}, no `target` anywhere. The constraint-name check therefore never matched, and BOTH concurrent requests got either a raw 500 or (worse) both would have raced past the intended graceful fallback. Fixed in this file's isUniqueViolation to also check meta.driverAdapterError.cause.originalMessage, keeping the old target check for forward-compat. Re-ran the same concurrent race after the fix: exactly one PredictionJob row, both requests returned the SAME jobId (one 201, one 200 'A job already exists for this idempotency key'). NOT FIXED (out of scope for this feature, flagged for follow-up): the identical bug in model-version.authorized.service.ts (breaks the intended clean 409 on a concurrent promote race, currently surfaces a raw 500 instead) and dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts's resolveOrCreateEditDraftService. Both should get the same fix.

Promote a new version DURING a running batch and confirm the output was scored end to end by the pinned version, asserted from the job row and the output's own recorded version — not inferred from timing. RESULT 2026-09-02, LIVE: submitted a batch pinned to ModelVersion v1 (PRODUCTION at submit time), paused its container before it could claim, promoted a real second ModelVersion v2 to PRODUCTION while v1's job sat paused (v1 -> ARCHIVED, confirmed via psql), then unpaused. The job claimed, scored, and completed successfully. Asserted from TWO independent sources, neither inferred from timing: (1) PredictionJob.modelVersionId in Postgres = v1's id, unchanged; (2) the container's OWN self-written batch_manifest.json in MinIO recorded modelVersionId = v1's id too. Never retargeted to v2 despite v2 being the live PRODUCTION version for the entire duration the container actually ran. getDescriptorByVersionIdService's no-stage-filter design (T05) confirmed correct against a real ARCHIVED-version resolution, not just unit-mocked.

features.title: POST /retrain — Trigger Only
features.blocked_on: RESOLVED 2026-09-01 BY TRANSCRIPTION (MODEL-SERVE-000-T05 / upstream re-read) — status flipped blocked -> pending. Upstream decisions.fine_tuning_undefined resolved 2026-08-25 (user decision): fine-tuning = a hyperparameter search — one algorithm, one artifact, one split, N hyperparameter sets in sequence, best kept by RMSE. features.description: An endpoint that records the intent to retrain and returns. The work is done by the existing trainer image, spawned the way MODEL-FLOW-003-T04 already spawns it. A successful retrain produces a new ModelVersion at STAGING and promotes nothing.

tasks.title: Define what retrain means, and write it in the shared decision
tasks.detail: This is the whole blocker and it is a product decision, not an engineering one. Everything below is unscopeable until it lands. Write the answer into MODEL-FLOW decisions.fine_tuning_undefined so both ledgers read one definition.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: Done by transcription, not new deliberation — see this feature's blocked_on and decisions.retrain_is_blocked_on_the_same_definition_as_fine_tuning: retrain = a hyperparameter search, one algorithm/artifact/split, N sets tried in sequence, best kept by RMSE.

tasks.title: Trigger endpoint with idempotency and a per-model lock
tasks.detail: Three clicks must not become three containers competing for the same 8 GiB. MODEL-FLOW-000-T03 established that /scratch's tmpfs shares the container's memory cgroup, so concurrent fits are not merely slow, they are a plausible OOM.
tasks.result_2026_09_03: POST /authorized/model/:modelId/retrain (ModelRetrainAuthorizedController, the same authorized/model/:modelId prefix model-version and prediction-job already use; a plain path, not '/retrain:trigger' — see MODEL-SERVE-003's find-my-way finding). TWO guards, not one: (1) the per-model LOCK is the partial unique index ModelCandidateJob_one_live_per_model, so the row is created FIRST and only the request that owns it reaches the spawn — a loser is refused before any container exists, which is what V02 actually measures; (2) idempotencyKey is opt-in and scoped (modelId, idempotencyKey), so a retry after a dropped response returns the ORIGINAL job even after it finished. The P2002-by-constraint-name check is copied from prediction-job.authorized.service.ts (the FIXED shape reading meta.driverAdapterError.cause.originalMessage), NOT from model-version.authorized.service.ts, whose meta.target-only copy MODEL-SERVE-003 proved never matches on this Prisma version — that copy is still broken and is flagged below, not fixed here.

tasks.title: Spawn the existing trainer; never fit in the serving process
tasks.detail: Per decisions.training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.
tasks.result_2026_09_03: Nothing fits in-process. launchModelRun -> trackSpawn -> TrainningContainerAuthorizedService.spawn(runId, token) with the default MODE=train — the identical path a wizard run takes, including the 8 GiB memory cap and the /scratch tmpfs this task's own note worried about. The trigger returns 201 with a job id while the first container is still starting. Because a retrain candidate is an ordinary ModelTrainingRun, the boot-time reconcileOrphanedRuns sweep re-attaches a retrain run after a backend restart with NO new code — the gap MODEL-FLOW-011-T04 closed applies here for free.

tasks.title: On success, create a STAGING version — promote nothing
tasks.detail: Auto-promotion would put an unreviewed model in front of live traffic on a schedule, which is a decision no one made. MODEL-SERVE-001-T03 takes the same position for Save Model, for the same reason.
tasks.result_2026_09_03:
advanceJobForRun's completion branch now forks on owner: a draft-owned job points ModelDraft.currentRunId at the winner (unchanged); a model-owned job calls completeModelOwnedJob, which mints a ModelVersion at the schema default STAGING from the winning run and writes resultVersionId. It reads nothing about PRODUCTION and writes nothing to it.

The compare-and-swap updateMany and the modelVersion.create are ONE interactive transaction, unlike the draft branch's two statements. The draft branch tolerates a crash between them (the next read re-derives); a retrain cannot — getJobService only reconciles QUEUED/RUNNING, so a job left SUCCEEDED with resultVersionId null would have lost its only deliverable with nothing able to repair it. getRunManifest (an HTTP call to apps/python for model_sha256/framework_versions) is read BEFORE the transaction opens, Save Model's own ordering. Re-entrancy uses ModelVersion.sourceRunId @unique: the transaction looks for an existing version for that run and ADOPTS it rather than racing the constraint. A winner with no modelKey fails the job with a named reason instead of minting a version that could never be loaded.

tasks.title: Compare the candidate against the incumbent, and publish the comparison
tasks.detail: The comparison is only meaningful on a common evaluation basis; a retrain on a widened window has a different test split, so a raw R² delta is not a like-for-like number. State the basis alongside the numbers rather than presenting a delta that reads as one and is not — the same discipline MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 applies to publishing the holdout's missing rate beside every metric.
tasks.result_2026_09_03: PREMISE CORRECTED AGAINST T01, the fourth time this ledger's own re-audit has had to do that. T05 was written while 'retrain' might still have meant a refit on a widened window, and it worried that a delta across two different test splits reads like a like-for-like number and is not. T01's resolution deleted that case: a retrain reuses the incumbent's artifact, target and split, so the delta IS like-for-like. What T05 asks for survives as a CHECK rather than a caveat — GET /authorized/model/:modelId/retrain/:jobId publishes a `comparison` block whose `basis` names goldArtifactId, artifactChecksum, targetY and the split, and `rmseDelta` is emitted ONLY when all four match between the candidate's run and the incumbent's. Otherwise comparable:false carries the reason, rmseDelta is null, and BOTH raw numbers are still published. RMSE leads and r2 is reported beside it, never used to rank (the observed r2 = -1,110,858 run is why). Both directions were exercised live — see V04.

acceptance_criteria: The endpoint returns immediately with a job id and never fits in-process.
Concurrent triggers for one model produce one job.
A successful retrain creates a STAGING version and changes no PRODUCTION pointer.
The candidate-versus-incumbent comparison states its evaluation basis, and refuses to present a delta across incomparable bases as if it were one.

features.implementation:
Built 2026-09-03, backend only — no client wiring (not asked for; apps/client/lib/retrain.ts's 700ms setTimeout simulation and use-model-retrain.ts stay exactly as they are, and that file's own comment 'Retraining is a simulation today (no training infra yet)' is now the only stale thing left, flagged not fixed). NO new orchestrator and NO trainer-image change: a retrain is a ModelCandidateJob owned by a Model instead of a ModelDraft, so it runs on the SAME advanceJobForRun compare-and-swap chain MODEL-FLOW-005/013 already live-verified, and each candidate is an ordinary ModelTrainingRun spawned by the SAME MODE=train path (soft-sensor-trainer 1.0.6 untouched, no tag bump — the search is orchestrated ABOVE the container, as schema.prisma's own ModelCandidateJob comment states).

Extraction, not duplication, three times over (the discipline MODEL-FLOW-005 established when it split createDraftRunService): (a) ModelRunLaunchAuthorizedService.createRunService -> assertModelAccess + new public launchModelRun(modelId, dto, candidateJobId?), the no-user/no-role write a webhook-driven chained candidate needs; (b) the ModelVersion field mapping out of Save Model's inline tx.modelVersion.create into @/lib/model-version-from-run (buildModelVersionData + nextModelVersionNumber), so Save Model's version 1 and a retrain's max+1 differ in exactly one field and cannot drift; (c) getJobService's reconcile-on-read + per-candidate table into reconcileAndShape, called by both the wizard's GET and the retrain GET.

Schema: modelDraftId nullable + modelId/sourceVersionId/resultVersionId/idempotencyKey added, with a hand-written XOR CHECK (ModelCandidateJob_owner_exactly_one) and two hand-written partial unique indexes (ModelCandidateJob_one_live_per_model, ModelCandidateJob_idempotency_key) — the same hand-written-partial-index precedent this table already carries for the draft owner. sourceVersionId/resultVersionId are bare Strings with NO foreign key, deliberately: an FK there would add a third edge to the Model -> ModelVersion/ModelTrainingRun cascade diamond that broke deleteModelService once (MODEL-SERVE-001's ModelVersion_sourceRunId_fkey). V03 was added to this feature to prove that delete still works rather than assume it.

REAL BUG CAUGHT WHILE WIRING, not by review: getJobService rebuilt a candidate's loss-history key as draftRunKey(job.modelDraftId, run.id, 'loss_history.json'). For a model-owned job that is 'drafts/null/runs/…', which soft-fails to null and would have silently shown NO loss history on every retrain candidate. Fixed by reading the STORED run.lossHistoryKey (written by complete()'s buildRunKey(owner,…), correct for either owner) — the same 'read the pinned key, never re-derive it' rule MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 established for featureSpecKey. The draft path is unaffected either way.

One narrowing recorded rather than discovered later: an incumbent fitted with expanding-window CV is REFUSED (422, reason named). A job row carries one trainTestSplit ratio, and a CV incumbent has no single ratio to reuse — reconstructing one would retrain on a different basis than the version it claims to improve on, exactly what T05 exists to prevent.

features.title: Prediction Logging and Drift Signal
features.description: Record inputs and predictions so that a model going wrong is observable, and so that a future automatic retrain has a trigger that is a measurement rather than a calendar.

tasks.title: Log request features, prediction and version to the time-series store
tasks.detail: Sampled, not every request — full-fidelity logging of a high-rate soft sensor is a second data pipeline nobody planned for. State the sampling rate; a rate chosen by accident makes every downstream statistic uninterpretable.
tasks.result_2026_09_03: PredictionLog Prisma model (packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma) + hand-written migration 20260903120000_model_serve_005_prediction_log; apps/serving samples per-REQUEST (SERVING_LOG_SAMPLE_RATE, default 1.0) and caps per-request detail rows (SERVING_LOG_MAX_ROWS, default 200) while computing aggregates over the FULL request regardless of the cap; every logged row records the sampling rate that was actually in force, on the row, never re-derived from current config later. New backend module prediction-log/ (PredictionLogIngestAuthorizedController under authorized/serving, ServingTokenGuard) and apps/python's prediction_log_service.append write the object to serving-logs/{modelId}/{modelVersionId}/dt=.../hour=.../{uuid}.parquet. Bounded so logging can never fail or delay /predict — verified in the unit suite, not just asserted.

REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE BUILDING ON IT, not part of the original task list: schemas/preprocess.py's TagColumnStats never declared `median`/`std`, so FastAPI's own response_model silently stripped both from every GET .../column-stats response even though column_stats.json has carried them since DS-LAKE-005B-A-T07 and three downstream layers (dataset-version.authorized.dto.ts's TagColumnStatsSchema, the client's ArtifactTagColumnStats type, dataset-detail-sheet.tsx's own rendering) already assumed they arrived. Fixed at the source (added both fields), additive, verified with a direct construct/dump round-trip.

Design, decided with the user before building: bytes in MinIO (serving-logs/{modelId}/{modelVersionId}/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/hour=HH/{uuid}.parquet, one object per SAMPLED request), index+aggregates in Postgres (new PredictionLog model — objectKey?, objectChecksum?, rowCount, loggedRows, samplingRate, featureStats Json, predictionStats Json, requestedAt). Write path is serving -> backend -> python: apps/serving holds no Postgres/MinIO credentials by design (decisions already on record for MODEL-SERVE-002), so it computes its aggregates locally over the SAME model-ready frame `to_model_ready` already produced (rows_to_predictions now returns `(predictions, scaled)`, not `predictions` alone — its one caller and its tests moved with it) and POSTs a capped raw-row sample plus the aggregates to a new ServingTokenGuard route; the backend forwards only the capped rows to python for the actual object write (apps/python's new prediction_log_service.append/series, plus ObjectStore.list_object_keys, added because nothing public exposed listing before this) and stores the aggregates straight to Postgres itself — python never sees or computes an aggregate. Logging is scheduled via FastAPI BackgroundTasks AFTER the /predict response would already be built, and every step from there is wrapped so a broken/unreachable log sink can never fail or delay the response — live-verified in the unit suite by monkeypatching the log POST to raise a real requests.ConnectionError and asserting /predict still returns 200 with correct predictions.

T02's drift math (apps/backend/src/lib/prediction-drift.ts, pure functions, no I/O): poolFeatureStats combines many requests' sufficient statistics into one exact pooled mean/variance; computeDrift compares that against column_stats.json's mean/std (exact z-score) and ESTIMATES an out-of-range rate via a Normal-CDF approximation against the baseline's own empirical p1/p99 bounds — stated as an estimate, not a count, because PredictionLog stores sufficient statistics, not raw values, so an exact per-value out-of-range rate would need either every raw value (defeats the point of aggregating) or a running histogram this schema does not carry. Thresholds (warnSd 1.5 / criticalSd 3.0 / outOfRangePct 10) reuse the wizard's own field names (MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's list) but are system-wide env defaults in this pass, not persisted per model — MODEL-SERVE-006-T09 is explicitly where those atoms get a real per-model home.

features.title: Scheduled Hourly Inference — Windows, Logs, and the Monitoring Record
features.description: Run a promoted model on a fixed cadence, writing one predictions parquet and one metrics document per time window, with per-run logs readable afterwards. This is the feature that makes 'deployed' mean something. It needs no serving process — see decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference.

findings: THE UNIT IS A TIME WINDOW, NOT A TICK. A scheduler written as 'every hour, read the latest values, predict' loses data permanently on every miss, cannot say which hours are missing, and has no backfill path. A scheduler written as 'ensure a row exists for every window' gets gap detection, backfill and idempotency from one UNIQUE constraint. This is the single decision the whole feature rests on.

SCHEDULED WORK HAS NO CALLER, WHICH CHANGES WHAT FAILURE MEANS. A sync request that fails returns an error to someone who is waiting. A window that fails is observed by nobody. So the feature is not complete when windows succeed — it is complete when a window that DOESN'T run is visible. Hence T10, which is the one task here that must not be cut.

setInterval().unref() IS ADEQUATE HERE, BUT FOR A DIFFERENT REASON THAN IT WAS ADEQUATE FOR THE SWEEPER. MODEL-FLOW-011-T03 chose it because a missed sweep costs nothing — next tick does the work. A missed inference window is a permanent gap. It is still adequate, but ONLY because the tick's job is an idempotent insert keyed on window_start, so a later tick recovers what an earlier one missed. If the tick ever predicts directly, this mechanism becomes wrong.

PI TAGS DO NOT ARRIVE TOGETHER AND THE LAB TARGET ARRIVES MUCH LATER. window_end = now() yields a frame that is structurally complete and factually empty in places — and the model will score it without error, because the columns exist. This is the same mechanism MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 records for the holdout (no imputation, so a hole reaches predict() and depresses the result with no trace), except it recurs every hour instead of once. Hence a deliberate lag (T04) and a per-window missing rate (T05).

A PROMOTE MID-SERIES IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PROCESS CHANGE UNLESS THE VERSION IS PINNED PER WINDOW. Two adjacent points from different model versions render as a step change on the same axis as a real process shift, and someone will spend days on the wrong hypothesis. Pinning also yields shadow evaluation for free: two rows, same window, different versions.

tasks.title: InferenceWindow entity, keyed on (modelVersionId, windowStart)
tasks.detail:
Fields: modelId, modelVersionId, windowStart, windowEnd, status (PENDING|RUNNING|SUCCEEDED|FAILED|SKIPPED), predictionsKey, metricsKey, inputRows, missingPct, imageDigest, runId, startedAt, finishedAt, failureReason.

UNIQUE (modelVersionId, windowStart) IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. It is the idempotency mechanism, so this feature needs no idempotency key of the kind MODEL-SERVE-003-T02 requires — windowStart is the natural key and a repeated insert is a no-op. It also makes gaps queryable (status != 'SUCCEEDED') and makes backfill an insert rather than a code path.

SKIPPED is a real terminal status, not a synonym for FAILED: a window with too few input rows to score was correctly not attempted, and conflating it with a failure would make the staleness alarm cry wolf on a quiet plant.

tasks.title: The tick inserts windows and nothing else
tasks.detail:
setInterval(...).unref() in onModuleInit, matching MODEL-FLOW-011-T03's mechanism and PreprocessingJobService.scheduleStragglerSweep's precedent. Env-configurable, <= 0 disables.

The tick does exactly two things: insert PENDING rows for windows that have none, and reconcile rows stuck in RUNNING past a timeout. IT MUST NOT SCORE ANYTHING. Scoring in the tick reintroduces every property this design exists to avoid — a missed tick becomes a lost window, the interval becomes load-bearing, and a slow run delays the next one. Errors logged and swallowed; anything the tick missed is still eligible next time, which is only true because of T01's key.

tasks.title: infer.py as a second entrypoint on the existing trainer image
tasks.detail:
Reads its window spec from a /claim-style callback exactly as train.py does, resolves the model object and scaler state (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 must have answered where scalers live — this task is blocked in practice until it has), scores, writes predictions.parquet and metrics.json, reports through /log and /complete.

Same image as the trainer so both entrypoints unpickle with the same library versions, and so image_digest provenance works identically. HEED MODEL-FLOW-000-T04's warning: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile, so a correct repo and a stale deployed image are indistinguishable today. Adding an entrypoint makes that worse, because a deployed image without infer.py fails in a way that looks like a scheduler bug. Add the CI build in this task, not later.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: UNBLOCKED: MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 answered where scalers live — feature_spec.json's scalingParams, one hop off ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey, applied via the existing to_model_ready(..., fitted_params=...). infer.py resolves scaler state the same way T05/T06 above do. Also inherits the serving-host finding: the Docker-daemon spawn this entrypoint runs under is now verified adequate for short-lived containers (decisions.serving_host_undecided, closed for MODEL-SERVE-006).

tasks.title: Window boundaries from a chosen ingestion lag
tasks.detail:
windowEnd = now() - lag, where lag is a configured value someone decided, per model. Do NOT default it to zero and do not derive it from the cadence — freshness and completeness genuinely trade against each other here and the trade must be made deliberately.

Measure before choosing: the 8 tags in the observed run's feature_columns (AI001A2.PV, AI206.PV, TI202/203/205/206/207.PV, Spgr_in_feed_Header_1) against RYGPDH01, worst-case arrival. The lab target's own latency is a different and much longer number and belongs to T08, not here — inference needs features only.

tasks.title: Record inputRows and missingPct per window
tasks.detail: On the row, not only inside the output object, so a series query can join them without opening parquet. Without this, a prediction series that starts wandering is indistinguishable between real process drift and a sensor that stopped reporting — and the second is far more common. Same rule and same reason as MODEL-FLOW-010-T06's insistence that the holdout's missing rate be published beside every figure.

tasks.title: Partitioned output layout for the monitoring record
tasks.detail:
inference/{modelId}/{modelVersionId}/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/hour=HH/predictions.parquet, plus metrics.json alongside. Hive-style so a date range reads without listing everything.

KEPT SEPARATE FROM drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/predictions.parquet ON PURPOSE: that object is the test-split prediction, immutable and backward-looking; this one is an append-only operational record with different retention and a different access pattern. Also a different root from drafts/, which the findings note is already shared by two entities.

Do not couple the read path to one-file-per-hour. 8,760 objects per model-year is fine for MinIO and slow to scan; daily compaction is not needed on day one but becomes needed, and a reader that assumes hourly files has to be rewritten then.

tasks.title: Pin modelVersionId at window creation, and expose version boundaries
tasks.detail: Already in T01's key; this task is the read side. Any series rendering must be able to say where a version changed, because the alternative is a step change attributed to the process. Falls out for free: two rows for one windowStart under different versions is a shadow comparison, which is the safe way to exercise a candidate — including the current r2 = -2.4068 model — without promoting it.

tasks.title: Metric registry — derived from predictions, recomputable, selectable from the UI
tasks.detail:
Per decisions.metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not_computed_at_fit. One definition set, applied to test-split predictions for evaluation and to window predictions for monitoring, so the two are the same number computed the same way.

Each registry entry declares whether it is BACKFILLABLE from (actual, predicted) plus run_manifest scalars, or requires inputs not retained. That flag is not documentation — it is what stops a comparison table silently mixing metrics that exist for all history with metrics that exist only for new runs.

mpSelectedMetricsAtom becomes a real selection over this registry instead of a filter over browser-computed values. THAT SUBSTITUTION IS ONLY MEANINGFUL AFTER MODEL-FLOW-004 (see findings): applied to today's phase-3-evaluation.tsx it would change which locally-computed numbers are displayed and nothing else.

tasks.title: Persist the schedule, and adopt the existing deploy atoms rather than new ones
tasks.detail:
Per-model schedule config: enabled, cadence, lag (T04), and the five fields phase-4-deploy.tsx already holds unpersisted in the store — autoRetrain, warnSd, criticalSd, driftMonitor, driftThresholdPct (per MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's field list). USE THOSE NAMES. A parallel set means the wizard and the scheduler describe the same setting in two vocabularies, and reconciling them later is worse than adopting them now.

This is the change that lets phase-4-deploy.tsx render those controls honestly, which its own comment declines to do today for the stated reason that nothing persists them.

tasks.title: Staleness alarm on the absence of successful windows
tasks.detail:
If no window has reached SUCCEEDED for longer than a configured multiple of the cadence, raise it. DO NOT CUT THIS TASK. Every other task in this feature makes the monitoring record trustworthy; this is the only one that reveals when the record has stopped being written. A drift dashboard with no incoming data looks calm, and calm is exactly the wrong signal.

SKIPPED windows must not silence the alarm and must not trigger it either — they are a legitimate quiet plant, and treating them as either extreme makes the alarm useless in one direction or the other.

tasks.title: Backfill by inserting windows, with no separate code path
tasks.detail: A range request inserts PENDING rows for windows that have none. The worker cannot distinguish backfill from live, which is the point — a second code path is a second set of bugs, and it would be exercised only during incidents. T01's UNIQUE constraint means over-requesting a range is harmless.

tasks.title: Derive deployStatus from the last successful window
tasks.detail:
Per decisions.deploy_status_currently_asserts_something_untrue. Today `updateModel(modelId, { deployStatus: 'running' })` writes a claim nothing backs. Once windows exist, that claim has a real referent and must be READ from it, not written beside it. Leaving both means two sources of truth for 'is this deployed', and the stale one wins whenever someone forgets to update it.

Phase-4-deploy.tsx's own structure survives this change unharmed: deploy stays a second write after save, and a failed deploy still leaves a saved model. What changes is that the second write enables a schedule instead of setting a string.

acceptance_criteria: A promoted model produces one predictions object and one metrics document per window, on the configured cadence, with no manual action.
Every window is queryable by its own boundaries, and windows that did not succeed are listable as gaps.
A missed or failed window can be backfilled by requesting its range, through the same worker that runs live windows.
Requesting an already-present window is a no-op — enforced by a unique constraint, not by a service check.
Each window records the model version that scored it, pinned at creation, and a series can show where the version changed.
Each window records its input row count and missing rate on the row itself.
Window boundaries respect a configured ingestion lag; the lag is a chosen value, not a default of zero.
Per-window logs are readable after the container exits, through the same path training logs already use.
The absence of successful windows raises an alarm; SKIPPED windows neither raise nor suppress it.
Evaluation and monitoring metrics come from one registry applied to stored predictions, and each entry states whether it is backfillable.
Adding a metric to the registry requires no retraining and no refit to populate it for past runs — for backfillable entries.
deployStatus is derived from the last successful window; no caller sets it directly.
The schedule reuses the field names the wizard's existing deploy atoms already use.

verification.description: THE ONLY TEST THAT DISTINGUISHES A WORKING SCHEDULER FROM ONE THAT HAS NOT YET MISSED: stop the scheduler for three cadence periods, restart it, and confirm all three absent windows are (a) visible as gaps, (b) backfillable, and (c) that backfilling them produces output indistinguishable from live windows. A test that only asserts normal windows succeed cannot tell these apart.

Kill the backend mid-window, restart, and confirm the row reaches a terminal status rather than staying RUNNING. This is MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's observed orphan, reproduced deliberately at a cadence where it will recur. If MODEL-FLOW-011-T04 has not landed, this verification fails by design and is the evidence that the dependency is real.

Run a window against data with a KNOWN hole in one feature tag, and confirm both that missingPct records it and that the prediction is not silently produced as if the frame were complete. Running against clean data proves only that the happy path works, which is not what T05 exists for.
Promote a new version between two windows and confirm the series exposes the boundary — asserted from the pinned modelVersionId on each row, not inferred from timestamps.

Add a backfillable metric to the registry and confirm it populates for a run that predates the addition, with NO retraining. Then attempt the same with an entry marked not-backfillable and confirm it is reported as unavailable for that run rather than computed from something it should not use.

Enable a schedule, let one window succeed, then disable the model's schedule and confirm deployStatus changes with the record rather than remaining whatever was last written. A status that can only be set forward is the bug this checks for.

Insert two windows for one windowStart under two different versions and confirm both score and store independently — the shadow-evaluation path T07 claims comes for free, verified rather than assumed.

findings:
CORRECTED (a) — `datasets/` IS THE BUCKET NAME, NOT A PREFIX. The module docstring renders the layout as `datasets/{datasetId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/data.parquet`, which reads as a prefixed key and is what an earlier draft of this feature assumed. The key helpers disagree: artifact_prefix returns f"{dataset_id}/artifacts/{artifact_id}/", version_key returns f"{dataset_id}/{version_id}.parquet", tmp_key returns f"{dataset_id}/tmp/...". Dataset keys begin with a BARE UUID and have no named root at all. The only named roots in the store are models/, drafts/ and feature-presets/.

CONSEQUENCE: a key-to-bucket resolver cannot dispatch on the first segment, because dataset keys have nothing there to dispatch on. It must dispatch on the roots that DO exist and treat rootless keys as the dataset default. The docstring should also be fixed to say `bucket / key` — it is the direct cause of this misreading and will cause it again.

CONFIRMED — `drafts/` IS SHARED, AND THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE THIRD SEGMENT. Previously inferred from one observed gold_object_key; now confirmed against the code. drafts/{id}/runs/{id}/… is a model run output (draft_run_key, MODEL-FLOW-003-T08) and drafts/{id}/artifacts/{id}/… is a dataset draft artifact (the observed gold_object_key). is_draft_run_key already tests exactly this shape — 4 segments after the root with parts[1] == 'runs' — so the discriminator a resolver needs is a predicate that already exists and is already tested.

CORRECTED (b) — THERE ARE NO HARDCODED BUCKET LITERALS, AND THE CONSTRUCTOR ALREADY TAKES A BUCKET. An earlier draft budgeted an audit for scattered literals. There are none: self.bucket is set once in __init__ from settings.S3_BUCKET and every method reads that one attribute (~15 sites, all reads). ObjectStore.__init__ already accepts an explicit `bucket` argument.

So multi-bucket is NOT a signature change threaded through fifteen methods — it is a FACTORY returning a per-bucket instance, plus a change at the few places that construct or hold an ObjectStore. _presign_minio is already an instance-level cache, which fits per-bucket instances rather than fighting them. This is materially cheaper than the earlier estimate and is the single biggest correction in this pass.

CORRECTED (c) — A BUCKET LIFECYCLE RULE CANNOT EXPRESS THE `models` RETENTION RULE, AND THE CODEBASE ALREADY SAYS SO. ensure_tmp_lifecycle_rule's own docstring: committed artifact prefixes are never expressed there because they need a reference check 'which a bucket lifecycle rule cannot do — only application-level cleanup is authoritative'. 'Retained while referenced' is exactly that kind of check.

This feature's original rationale — separation makes retention expressible at the bucket level — is therefore HALF WRONG and is restated: separation does not express the right rule, it prevents a wrong rule from REACHING the wrong objects. That is still worth having, and it is a narrower claim than the one first made.

THE TAG MECHANISM FOR THIS PROBLEM ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS BUILT FOR THE SAME REASON. TMP_LIFECYCLE_TAG_KEY's doc comment explains that S3/MinIO Prefix filters are literal and anchored, never wildcards, so 'tmp/ under any dataset' is not expressible as a prefix rule — hence an object TAG plus one bucket-wide rule. The identical constraint applies to a models bucket holding BOTH models/… and drafts/…/runs/… : two roots, so no single Prefix rule covers it, so a tag is needed there too. Any option chosen in T01 should reuse this mechanism rather than invent a second one.

PRIOR DECISION AGAINST A SECOND BUCKET, WITH A STATED REASON. PRESET_ROOT's comment: a prefix inside the existing bucket 'rather than a bucket of its own: ensure_bucket() has no runtime caller in this service, so a second bucket would need new bootstrap while a prefix needs none.' Confirmed: ensure_bucket has no automatic caller, and ensure_tmp_lifecycle_rule's comment records that docker-compose.yml does not declare MinIO at all — it runs as an uncommitted minio-local container. So every bucket is a manual, undocumented per-environment ops step.

This feature must engage with that decision rather than step around it. What presets did not have, and inference does, is a DIFFERENT RETENTION CLASS — presets and datasets are both reclaimable-with-a-reference-check, whereas an inference record is never reclaimable. That is a reason the earlier decision did not weigh, not a reason to overrule it.

`models/` MAY HAVE NO LIVE OBJECTS AT ALL. MODEL_ROOT, model_run_prefix and model_run_key all exist, but MODEL-FLOW-003-T08 routed live writes to draft_run_key, and MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 adopts by pointer without moving bytes — so nothing may ever write under models/. UNVERIFIED (needs a bucket listing), but if true, a 'models' bucket would hold only drafts/…/runs/… keys, which is confusing enough to be worth knowing before naming anything.

tasks.title: DECIDE the retention-class mechanism — three options, one recommendation
tasks.detail:
This was drafted as 'define three buckets'. Findings (c) and the PRESET_ROOT precedent make that a choice rather than a conclusion, so it is recorded as one.

OPTION A — three buckets (datasets / models / inference). Strongest isolation: a lifecycle rule or access grant scoped to a bucket cannot reach another class even if authored carelessly. Costs what PRESET_ROOT's comment names: two more manual bucket-creation steps in an environment where MinIO is not even in docker-compose, plus the factory from T02.

OPTION B — one bucket, retention-class OBJECT TAG on every write, lifecycle rules keyed on tag. Matches the mechanism already proven here for tmp/, needs no bootstrap, no factory, no resolver. Weaker: nothing stops a rule authored against a prefix or against no filter at all from reaching every class, and the tag is only as good as the writer that sets it.

OPTION C (RECOMMENDED) — tag everything by retention class per Option B, AND give `inference` its own bucket. inference is the one class that is never reclaimable, grows without bound, and has zero existing objects — so its bucket is free, needs no migration, and is the one place where 'an operator cannot accidentally point a rule at this' is worth a manual bootstrap step. datasets and models stay co-located under tags, which keeps faith with the PRESET_ROOT decision instead of quietly reversing it.

WHICHEVER IS CHOSEN, RECORD IT AS A DECISION WITH ITS REJECTED ALTERNATIVES. The next person to face 'new bucket or new prefix' will read whatever is written here, the way this task read PRESET_ROOT's comment.

tasks.title: Tag every write with its retention class
tasks.detail:
Required under all three options in T01 — it is what makes the class legible to tooling at all, and under Option B it is the entire mechanism.

put_frame already sets an object tag conditionally (`if "/tmp/" in key`). Generalise that: derive the retention class from the key and tag every write, in put_object_stream so it covers put_frame and put_object_bytes together. put_json goes DIRECTLY to self._client.put_object and bypasses that path — the module's own comments flag it as un-refactored — so it needs the tag added too, or every JSON sidecar (including run_manifest.json) is written untagged.

Classes: SWEEPABLE (dataset drafts/artifacts, tmp, presets), REFERENCED (model run outputs), PERMANENT (inference records). Note that REFERENCED still cannot be enforced by a lifecycle rule — finding (c) — so its tag is a label for humans and audits, not an enforcement point. Say so where the constant is defined, or someone will write a rule against it and believe it works.

tasks.title: One key-to-class resolver, built on the predicates that exist
tasks.detail:
class_for_key(key) in object_store.py with its TS twin in artifact-keys.ts. Dispatch on the roots that actually exist, per finding (a) — NOT on the first segment, which is a bare UUID for dataset keys:

  inference/…                    → PERMANENT
  models/…                       → REFERENCED
  drafts/… + is_draft_run_key    → REFERENCED
  drafts/… + /artifacts/         → SWEEPABLE
  feature-presets/…              → SWEEPABLE
  anything else (rootless)       → SWEEPABLE

The drafts/ branch MUST call is_draft_run_key rather than re-deriving the segment test — the two would otherwise disagree about the same key and only one of them is under test.

The rootless default is not a fallback: it is the historically correct answer for every dataset object ever written, all of which are bucket-less and root-less by construction.

tasks.title: Per-bucket ObjectStore factory — only if T01 chooses A or C
tasks.detail:
Per finding (b) this is a factory, not a refactor: ObjectStore.__init__ already accepts `bucket`, and no method holds a literal. store_for(bucket) caching one instance per bucket name, plus store_for_key(key) composing it with T03's resolver.

THE REAL WORK IS AT THE CONSTRUCTION SITES, NOT IN THIS CLASS. artifact_service and its siblings hold a single ObjectStore today; a flow spanning classes (infer.py reads a model, reads the gold parquet, writes an inference record — three classes) needs the store resolved per key rather than per service. Audit who constructs one before changing anything.

Under Option C only `inference` is separate, so the factory has two entries and the blast radius is small. Under Option A every dataset read moves too, which is the expensive half.

tasks.title: Write inference/ into its chosen home from the very first object
tasks.detail:
Free today, a migration after MODEL-SERVE-006-T06 lands. Nothing has written an inference object yet.

Under Option A or C this means the bucket exists and is bootstrapped BEFORE the first scheduled window runs — and since ensure_bucket has no runtime caller (finding: PRESET_ROOT precedent), 'exists' means someone did it by hand and wrote down that they did. A scheduler whose first window fails on NoSuchBucket at 02:00 is the predictable version of this.

tasks.title: Add bucket and gold_artifact_id to run_manifest.json
tasks.detail:
gold_bucket makes the manifest self-describing — a reader years later needs no resolver to find the object. gold_artifact_id (b9e25f8d in the observed run) is the durable reference: it is ALREADY IN the key as a path segment, so this promotes a substring to a field. A reference parsed out of a path breaks when the path shape changes; a field does not.

Both, not either. A manifest lacking gold_bucket resolves via T03's default, which is correct for every manifest written so far.

NOTE the naming trap finding (a) created: gold_object_key's value is a KEY relative to a bucket, and the docstring's rendering of it as `datasets/...` is what made an earlier reading treat the bucket as part of the path. Fix that docstring in this task.

tasks.title: Write down each class's rule where an operator will see it
tasks.detail:
Per finding (c), state plainly what tooling CAN and CANNOT enforce: SWEEPABLE is expressible as a tag-filtered lifecycle rule (the tmp/ rule already proves the mechanism); PERMANENT is expressible as the absence of any rule; REFERENCED IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE and depends on MODEL-FLOW-011-T05's run-level guard plus ArtifactCleanupService.

Recording the limit is the point. A retention scheme that looks fully enforced but has one class enforced only by application code is more dangerous than one that admits it, because the next person will trust the appearance.

Also record the bootstrap steps T05 needs, since ensure_bucket has no automatic caller and MinIO is not in docker-compose.

acceptance_criteria: T01's mechanism is chosen and recorded as a decision with its rejected alternatives, engaging with PRESET_ROOT's prior 'prefix not bucket' reasoning rather than bypassing it.
No existing object is moved; no persisted key column and no already-written manifest is rewritten.
Every write carries a retention-class tag — including put_json's, which bypasses the shared PUT path today.
One resolver per language maps key to retention class, calling is_draft_run_key rather than re-deriving its segment test.
A rootless key resolves to the dataset class, documented as historically correct rather than as a fallback.
The first inference object is written to its chosen home, with any bootstrap step recorded.
run_manifest.json records both gold_bucket and gold_artifact_id; a manifest lacking gold_bucket still resolves.
The written retention rules state which classes tooling can enforce and which one it cannot.
A model saved before this feature and one saved after load by the same code path.

verification.description: THE MIGRATION-SAFETY TEST: load a model whose run predates this feature (run 61f9aa28 is real) and confirm it resolves correctly AND that model_sha256 verifies via checksum_of. A test using only post-change objects proves the new path works and says nothing about the objects that can actually break.

PROVE THE SHARED ROOT IS DISAMBIGUATED: resolve drafts/{id}/runs/{id}/model.joblib and drafts/{id}/artifacts/{id}/data_gold.parquet and confirm DIFFERENT classes. A resolver dispatching on the first segment sends both to the same place and passes any test that checks only one.
Resolve a rootless legacy key ({datasetId}/{versionId}.parquet, the version_key layout) and confirm the dataset class. Finding (a) exists because this shape was mis-assumed once already.

Write a JSON sidecar via put_json and assert the retention tag is present on the stored object. put_json bypasses the shared PUT path, so a tag added only to put_object_stream leaves every manifest and metrics document untagged — and passes any test that writes a parquet.

If T01 chose A or C: place the same key in two buckets with different bytes, confirm the loader lands on the intended one, and confirm checksum verification catches it when it does not. The guards are key-structural and bucket-blind, so the checksum is the only discriminator.

global_definition_of_done: A scheduled model produces one record per time window; a window that did not run is visible as a gap and backfillable through the same path a live window uses.
Evaluation and monitoring read one metric registry over stored predictions — adding a backfillable metric never requires a refit.
'Deployed' is derived from the monitoring record, never asserted by a caller.

A production model's fitted artifact and feature spec are retained and pinned for as long as any version references them — the model object and the spec it needs are two objects in different places, and losing either is the same outage.
A saved Model can be promoted to production and rolled back without building or deploying an image.
At most one PRODUCTION version exists per model, enforced by the database.
The transform applied at inference is the same code as the one applied at training — proven by scoring a training-set row through the live endpoint, not by inspection.
A model that cannot be served correctly (target-derived features without history, framework mismatch, bad checksum) is refused at load or at request, never served with a plausible wrong answer.
Batch results are delivered by reference; no result bytes and no presigned URLs pass through a log.
Job state survives a process restart.
Retrain produces a candidate; a human promotes it.
No feature in this ledger writes to any MODEL-FLOW wizard path, and no MODEL-FLOW feature is reopened to accommodate one.
